Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Henry dominated the Jaguars for years during his Tennessee Titans tenure, with his last year of playing the Jaguars twice resulting in 191 rushing yards and 6.6 yards per carry. He has found paydirt against the Jaguars time and time again, and he is off to another good season in 2026. Add in the season-ending injury to star nose tackle Davon Hamilton, and this is a tough matchup for the Jaguars' top-ranked run defense. With that said, I think the Jaguars manage to bottle Henry up. No running back with a minimum of five carries has averaged more than 4.0 yards per carry against the Jaguars this season, with Jonah Coleman leading the way at 3.9 yards per carry. Chase Brown had 1.1, TreVeyon Henderson had 2.9, and Jonathan Taylor had 2.9 as well. I think the Jaguars repeat against the Ravens, especially with no Lamar Jackson in the lineup. Keep this in mind: according to NextGenStats, "Henry is averaging 3.5 yards per carry without Lamar Jackson on the field this season, a full yard less than with Jackson on the field (4.5). Henry has also been stuffed more often without Jackson (22.9%) than with him (16.0%), and he has been less efficient at keeping drives on schedule, posting a 33.7% success rate without Jackson compared to 49.3% with him." picks.blurb: Jaguars-Ravens Week 9 Picks Roundup: Golden Chance in AFC is at Stake Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The lights of an island game on national telivision are here, and the stage is set for the Jacksonville Jaguars. There will not be any Trevor Lawrence-Lamar Jackson round three due to an injury to Jackson. We won't see Tyler Huntley either, with Ravens undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano set to make the start. But there will still be a big stage for the Jaguars, along with a big opportunity. The Jaguars are fighting through their own injuries , losing Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray to season-ending injuries during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Add in running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker being questionable, and the Jaguars are a bit dinged up themselves. But if the Jaguars can overcome the challenge of a road trip against a talented team on a short week, they can do more than prove their mettle. They can be 6-2 entering a stretch where they play the Tennessee Titans twice in a three-week span, giving them a chance to have real-deal playoff-clinching scenarios in December. How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis It is hard not to pick the Jaguars here, and they once again get a clean sweep. It feels weird on the Jaguars end of things, but that is because every game has stakes when you are a good team, and the Jaguars are indeed a good team. The Jaguars have a big chance to make some clear headway toward a potential No. 1 seed in the AFC. They are clumped together right now with the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but they have to get by a rookie quarterback tonight before facing Cam Ward twice and J.J. McCarthy. If the Jaguars go on a run, they could be 9-2 by right after Thanksgiving. That would make them far more than just contenders in the AFC, and it would start with beating Baltimore. Things could have gotten much more interesting had Jackson been available, but the Jaguars will instead face the dreaded backup quarterback in primetime. Weirdly enough, two of the six losses in the Liam Coen era have been to backup quarterbacks after the Jaguars lost to Jake Browning and Davis Mills a year ago. The only other quarterbacks to beat the Jaguars in the regular-season in that span: Sam Darnold, Matt Stafford, Bo Nix, and CJ Stroud. The Jaguars have beaten other backup and rookie quarterbacks in that span, defeating Jacoby Brissett, Cam Ward (twice), Brady Cook, Riley Leonard, and for some reason, Philip Rivers last season. This season, they have gotten wins against a few guys who have played in the Super Bowl in Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow, and Drake Maye. Add in wins against Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy and Stroud last year, and the argument thatg the Jaguars have beaten up on bad quarterbacks doesn't make much sense. The Jaguars are a good team, and I expect Anthony Campanile's defense to get after the Ravens' young passer. Campanile likes to blitz and pressure quarterbacks into intentionally throwing the ball quickly, which helps the defense dictate where the ball will go in coverage. When you know where the ball is going, you can make plays on it or tackle and rally and make stops like the Jaguars have done for two years. According to NextGenStats, Jacksonville has generated a 39.6% pressure rate this season (8th-highest), and its pressures have arrived in 2.43 seconds on average, the quickest in the NFL. Seven of Jacksonville's pressures have resulted in turnovers, tied for the most in the league, and the Jaguars have generated 31 unblocked pressures, tied for second-most. This means the Jaguars' pressures are leading to big plays on the back end, and they force the issue with opposing quarterbacks. Against a young quarterback and a running game that has lesser numbers without Lamar Jackson, I think the Jaguars win this game with field position and red-zone stops. Jaguars 30, Ravens 13. The Jacksonville Jaguars are expected to be without defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn quad. With the trade deadline approaching, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN noted that the Jaguars' need for a defensive tackle has been amplified due to the injury. He also reported that the belief in league circles was that the team would explore upgrades on the line before the injury. They went from needing a pass-rushing interior lineman to a player who can impact the game in both the pass and run. away.blurb: The Ravens’ battered offensive line should get a boost Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars with starting rookie right guard Vega Ioane, who missed last week’s game against the Buffalo Bills with a knee injury, set to return. “I feel really good,” Ioane, who suffered a sprained MCL, said earlier this week. “I am confident in my ability to be able to come out.” Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins (stinger/illness) missed Wednesday’s practice and is listed as questionable. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) was ruled out for a third straight game. For the AFC South-leading Jaguars, top running back Bhayshul Tuten could be a game-time decision, coach Liam Coen said. He didn’t practice this week because of ankle/foot injuries. Starting defensive end Travon Walker, the No.1 overall pick in 2022 who has three sacks this season, is questionable with a rib injury. Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey questions criticism, says fans ‘always freaking out’ Ravens No. 2 QB Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley out for season Ioane, the 14th overall pick this past April, did not have a designation on Wednesday’s injury report and was a full participant in both practices this week. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Lamar Jackson's Ravens Future Discussed by NFL Insider Amid Rumors on Contract Status
home.blurb: Jones noted that although it is "anyone's guess" when a contract extension may be reached, the two sides have to figure something out in the not-too-distant future. While he is a dynamic force when healthy, Jackson missed four games last season and has been limited to five games so far this season due to injury. Despite the fact that the Baltimore Ravens and quarterback Lamar Jackson have yet to agree to a new contract, there is reportedly mutual interest in the two sides remaining together long term. According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, "there is no reason to believe" Jackson won't be back with the Ravens next year, as the Ravens have publicly declared that they "love him and want to keep him long term." Jackson is only signed through 2027, and he is currently set to have a salary cap hit of $84.3 million next season. On top of that, $42.47 million in void-year cap hits are set to activate from 2028 to 2030. With all of that in mind, it would behoove the Ravens to sign Jackson to a new deal before the 2027 season since it would allow the organization to structure the deal in such a way that it would offer immediate cap relief. The 29-year-old Jackson is a four-time Pro Bowler, three-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL MVP who has spent his entire nine-year NFL career in Baltimore. ▶️ Full Ravens-Cowboys Recap 06:01 After an ankle injury cost him three games, Jackson returned to start against the Buffalo Bills last week, but he injured his thumb on the Ravens' first offensive play of the game. If that proves to be the case, the 4-5 Ravens may be hard-pressed to make the playoffs even after the acquisition of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals this week. That would mark Baltimore's second consecutive season outside the playoffs, largely due to Jackson's unavailability. home.headline: Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens had a rough afternoon, starting with the first offensive play of the game when quarterback Lamar Jackson hit Bills defender Greg Rousseau's arm, causing Jackson to suffer a thumb injury and not return. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley , also didn't last long. Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half and didn't return. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Huntley suffered a turf toe injury. Huntley and Jackson could both miss time, and Jackson is confirmed out for at least four weeks. Head coach Jesse Minter said postgame that Jackson will be placed on injured reserve and will undergo surgery on his right thumb. Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report Unlock the latest Heavy on Ravens news — direct to your inbox. This was Jackson first game back after he suffered an ankle injury against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 and missed the last three games. "Ravens QB Tyler "Snoop" Huntley suffered what is thought to be a turf toe injury today at Buffalo, per source," Schefter wrote on X. "He is expected to undergo an MRI tomorrow to determine how much time if any he could miss." Ravens Could Be Down Jackson and Huntley for a While The Ravens turned to quarterback Joe Fagnano after losing Huntley, and he had a tough afternoon, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Minter also said, "We'll see" on whether Jackson will miss the rest of the season. Huntley has started three games this season, and the Ravens are 1-2. The Ravens beat the Falcons in his first start of the season but lost the last two against the Browns and Bengals. Losing your starting quarterback and backup in the same game is never good. It's even worse when this happens during a short week. The Ravens will have a quick turnaround as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. The Jaguars are coming off a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday to move to 5-2. Baltimore might not have a chance to play Huntley even if he can go, since it's hard to come back from an injury on a shorter week with less than four full days to recover. It will also be difficult for the Ravens to bring in a quarterback to play on Thursday, even if they lack confidence in Fagnano. The Ravens might have to get by with Fagnano starting on Thursday, then reevaluate options when they have about 10 days off between their games against the Jaguars and the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Falcons Score Prediction for NFL Week 9 (Cincinnati Should Roll in International Matchup) Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The NFL’s international series returns on Sunday in Week 9, as the Cincinnati Bengals and MVP candidate Joe Burrow hit the road to take on the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. Michael Penix Jr. and the Falcons suffered a brutal loss in the rain against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8, and they’re now just 3-5 this season and facing an uphill battle to win the NFC South. They’re set as underdogs in this matchup despite being the “home” team against Cincy. Burrow and the Bengals survived an overtime score with the Tennessee Titans in Week 8, and they’re now 5-2 this season and in a great spot to win the AFC North. With the Baltimore Ravens taking a step back after Lamar Jackson’s injury, Burrow and the Bengals are favored to win the division and are inside 20/1 to win the Super Bowl. Can they take care of business in Madrid against a Falcons team that has been extremely hit or miss in 2026? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of NFL games, a fun way to help bettors decide on spread, moneyline and total wagers each week. And, we’re trying to hit a bunch of exact scores in the process. With the NFL heading to Madrid in Week 9, both the Bengals and Falcons need a win to keep themselves in the mix in their respective division races. Who has the edge on Sunday morning? Let’s take a look at my final score prediction for this standalone matchup in Week 9. Bengals vs. Falcons Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bengals -3 (-112) Falcons +3 (-108) Bengals: -155 Falcons: +130 52.5 (Over -112/Under -108) Cincinnati opened as a 3.5-point favorite in this matchup, but the line has moved down to just three ahead of Sunday’s battle. The Bengals and Falcons have also seen the total for this matchup rise by three points since opening at 49.5. Bengals vs. Falcons Score Prediction Each week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan picks every single game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s targeting the Bengals as the “road team” in this international matchup on Sunday: The Falcons' handful of impressive performances this season have convinced people this team is better than they are. They continue to have plenty of issues on both sides of the ball. Their defense has regressed after a strong start to the season, and Michael Penix Jr. displays accuracy issues on a weekly basis. He now ranks 32nd out of 35 starting quarterbacks this season in completion percentage over expected. play and 12th in defensive weighted EPA per play. Don't be fooled into thinking their defense is bad because of a down game against the Titans last week. They certainly aren't an elite unit, but an average defense is good enough to let the Cincinnati offense do its thing to win games. The most important aspect of the Bengals' defense is its ability to stop the run. They rank sixth in opponent rush success rate, and we've already seen the Falcons fail to produce offensively when facing strong run defenses like the Steelers' and Buccaneers'. The Falcons have one of the best wins of the season (over San Francisco) and yet there have been multiple weeks where this offense has been incapable of moving the ball. Through eight weeks, the Falcons are 3-3 when Penix plays and they rank just 26th in the league in EPA/Play on offense. Atlanta has a top-10 defense in EPA/Play, yet they couldn’t stop a Bucs team that didn’t complete a pass in Week 8. Burrow and the Bengals have one of the best offenses in the NFL, and I expect them to roll on Sunday with the AFC North crown certainly within reach. picks.headline: FalconsSI Staff Predictions are Split on Falcons vs. Bengals in Spain
picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Predictions are Split on Falcons vs. Bengals in Spain Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons are in Madrid, Spain, for an international Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. Atlanta is looking to get back into the win column against a Cincinnati team that has won three consecutive games. The Bengals present a difficult challenge for Atlanta, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Joe Burrow leads one of the NFL’s most productive offenses, featuring star wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. With injuries beginning to catch up with the Falcons , slowing down Cincinnati’s passing attack could be a major challenge. Atlanta’s offense will also need to deliver a strong performance against a Bengals defense that has struggled at times this season. Michael Penix Jr. and Bijan Robinson will be important pieces as the Falcons attempt to keep pace with Burrow and company in what could be a high-scoring international matchup. Here are the Falcons On SI staff’s predictions for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup. Garrett Chapman (4-4) The Falcons will have a difficult test on Sunday with the high-flying Bengals offense. They will score plenty of points in this one, and it will be on Michael Penix Jr. to match that production. Working in their favor is the fact that the Bengals are not an elite pressure team, so if they can keep the quarterback clean, then the Falcons could keep up. Atlanta usually wins one of these games they aren’t supposed to every year, and I think Atlanta can find a way to get to Joe Burrow a few times. It’ll be a high-scoring game, and the Falcons’ season survives one more week with a 34-30 win. Prediction: Falcons 34, Bengals 30 Gerald Thomas, III (3-5) Welcome to another week of the most unpredictable team in football. This game has all the makings of one the Falcons play up for. International game, and the Bengals have been rolling with three-straight wins. This game could make for fireworks. Cincy is pretty much the middle of the pack defensively, but has one of the top offenses in the league. So the Falcons will have opportunities to put points on the board too. But can their secondary keep up with the likes of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins? We have to wait and see if they prove it. Expect a high-scoring affair in Madrid, with the Bengals coming out victorious. Prediction: Bengals 38, Falcons 34 Darius Hayes (3-5) After picking the Falcons to win each of the last three games, I’m finally going against Atlanta this week. I believed the Falcons had opportunities to pick up wins in two of those matchups, but unfortunately, I was wrong. Heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Bengals, I think Joe Burrow and Cincinnati’s offense will be too much to handle, especially with Atlanta’s injuries beginning to catch up with them. I expect the Falcons to keep it close, but ultimately, I’m taking the Bengals to win 27-24. Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 24 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-5) As inconsistent as the Falcons are, they’ve consistently shown us that they will beat teams they have no business beating and lose to teams they have no business losing to. That makes this a great week to be playing one of the better teams in the league. Pattern recognition aside, there are several aspects of this matchup that make me hopeful. The obvious key to this game will be whether the Falcons can stop Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. But the Falcons have been one of the better pass defenses in the league; they now have a fully healthy secondary, and their best pass rusher is back from suspension, although he is questionable for Sunday. The offense will need a big bounce-back to pull off the upset. Michael Penix Jr. will try to rebound after his best Desmond Ridder impression last week. But I think the Falcons’ o-line will be just as inspired to have a great showing after getting dominated by the Buccaneers’ d-line last week. Ultimately, I have the Falcons pulling off the upset behind an inspired run game and some big plays from Jeff Ulbrich and his defense when it matters. Prediction: Falcons 33, Bengals 30 Scott Kennedy (3-5) I've said for years that trying to predict what the Atlanta Falcons are going to do is a good way to look like an idiot. General manager Ian Cunningham has helped fix that off the field by dutifully addressing needs in free agency and matching premium positions of need with his top draft picks. However, all is not fixed in less than a year. The team on the field remains maddeningly inconsistent because of talent and depth problems inherited by Cunningham and head coach Kevin Stefanski. The Falcons have the same record that I do when trying to predict the outcome of their games: 3-5. In each of their three wins, I've picked them to lose. So naturally, being an underdog in a foreign country is the type of game that makes the Falcons dangerous for Cincinnati. That said, I'm a creature of logic, and logic tells me the cracks in Atlanta's defense will be too much for the offense to overcome. Prediction: Bengals 30, Falcons 20 Published 4 hours ago DARIUS HAYES Darius has a Master's in Communications from Georgia State and has previous experience covering the Atlanta Falcons with 3 Point Conversion and covering the NFL with On SI. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Falcons bold predictions for NFL Madrid Game in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football F1 São Paulo GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Bengals vs. Falcons bold predictions for NFL Madrid Game in Week 9 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Thu, November 5, 2026 at 10:46 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL's international schedule is back on in Week 9. Cincinnati and Atlanta will do battle in Spain in a game that could deliver plenty of fireworks for fans. The NFL sent two incredible offensive teams to Madrid that could put up plenty of points. After all, exciting games like this one can really expand the league's footprint on the international stage. Both teams have quite a lot in common. They are both in extremely tight division races where just one win could propel them into first place. However, the difference between the AFC North and the NFC South is absolutely massive. Still, the Falcons have looked impressive at times throughout the season. Meanwhile, the Bengals have been fairly consistent now that their defense is finally looking solid. Though they did not look good against the Titans last week. Regardless, both teams are hungry for a win and have all the offensive weapons needed to get it done. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? And will this game become an offensive shootout or a defensive struggle? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this huge international clash between the Bengals and Falcons in Madrid. Joe Burrow has a repeat of his Week 8 offensive explosion against the Falcons Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Bengals looked like a vintage version of the team in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Yes, Cincinnati did get the win. But it was shocking how much they needed to lean on Burrow to get the job done. Fortunately, Burrow is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL and passed that tough test with flying colors. Burrow finished 38-of-48 for 462 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. He also had one rushing touchdown. The veteran quarterback simply put the team on his back and willed them to victory. Now Burrow and friends must face an average Falcons defense that's allowed 223.4 passing yards per game this season. Keep in mind that the best opponent Atlanta has faced this season is Chicago. In that game, Caleb Williams shredded their secondary for 305 passing yards. Beyond that game, the Falcons have not been tested very much through the air this season. So just how much damage could Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins do against the Falcons? Burrow will have a repeat performance from last week, going over 400 passing yards and throwing at least three touchdown passes. Cincinnati has to throw the ball to win right now, so they'll be comfortable going guns blazing. To make this even bolder, both Higgins and Chase will each go over 100 receiving yards and score a touchdown. Bijan Robinson will have twice as many rushing yards as the Bengals The disparity between Atlanta and Cincinnati's running game is absolutely massive. Cincinnati has one of the worst rushing attacks in the entire league. In fact, they only average 80.3 rushing yards per game so far this season. That average is quite concerning since they've already played in seven games, so a few bad performances aren't dragging it down. Chase Brown and company just aren't getting the job done. Atlanta is the exact opposite, with their Bijan Robinson-led rushing attack as one of the best in the NFL. They've averaged 134.8 rushing yards per game this year. Only the Buccaneers, Bears, and Bills have a better average. Robinson is the main reason why the Falcons have such a huge advantage on the ground. Just how good will he do in comparison to the Bengals in Madrid? Bijan is averaging 100.6 rushing yards per game in 2026. He is single-handedly outperforming the Bengals on the ground despite failing to break 100 rushing yards in four consecutive games. The Falcons know that they need Robinson to pop off if they want a chance to win this game. They'll design a game plan to do exactly that, and it has a great chance to work. Bijan won't just have more rushing yards than the Bengals, he'll double them up. All it would take is an elite game by Robinson and a pass-happy attack from Cincinnati's offense. Falcons, Bengals combine for at least 80 points in an exciting shootout in Madrid Image Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images This game has all the necessary ingredients of an offensive shootout. Burrow and friends should have no problem scoring at will in this game. Bijan and the Falcons have a huge advantage running the ball. That should keep their offense consistent throughout this game, even if the Bengals start running up the score. Make no mistake, the Bengals have a solid defense that is both frisky and opportunistic. They won't be playing to their strengths when going up against Bijan on the ground. But once the offense gets established, Cincinnati could start to pull away. They should come away with the victory as long as nothing too fluky happens. The Bengals will come out on top thanks to their high-powered offense than can score at the drop of a hat. If they need points late in this game, they will make it happen. The same is not true for the Falcons. Related: NFL picks, predictions, odds for Week 9: Can home dogs bite? Related: NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 2026 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: D/ST

(Injury Update, Betting Impact for Titans vs. Bengals in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase dealt with an ankle injury early in the week, missing some practice time, but he's off the injury report and expected to play on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) said he's good to go for Week 8, via @char_cliff . That's great news for the Bengals and quarterback Joe Burrow, as Cincy is off to a 4-2 start and has a real case to win the AFC North in the 2026 season. Chase and Tee Higgins have been the driving forces in this Bengals offense that is seventh in the NFL in EPA/Play and fifth in EPA/Pass. The Titans rank in the bottom 10 in the NFL in passing yards allowed this season, and they just moved on from their top defensive player -- defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons -- ahead of the trade deadline. So, oddsmakers are expecting a big game from Chase and this Bengals offense. This season, Chase has 32 receptions on 45 targets for 351 yards and five scores. While he has less receiving yards than Higgins, Chase has still be an important part of Cincy's attack, receiving nine or more targets in three of his six games. Here's a look at how I'm betting on him in the prop market in this Week 8 showdown. Best Ja'Marr Chase Prop Bet vs. Titans in NFL Week 8 Ja'Marr Chase Anytime TD (-120) Chase may not have the monster receiving yards numbers that we've grown accustomed to seeing, but the star wideout has been a touchdown machine, scoring in four of his six gmaes. He's found the end zone in back-to-back weeks since exiting Week 4 early with a concussion. Burrow has thrown 11 touchdown passes in his last four games, including back-to-back games with four touchdown passes. So, he should be able to find Chase quite easily against a Tennessee defense that is 26th in the league in EPA/Pass despite allowing just six passing scores in 2026. Chase is one of the few receivers in the NFL that is truly matchup-proof, and I expect him to continue his strong start to the 2026 season on Sunday. away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. home.headline: Reports: Colts have gotten interest on QB Daniel Jones
home.blurb: Interim general manager Ed Dodds has had discussions with other teams regarding Jones, according to ESPN and NFL Network. It isn’t known whether Dodds reached out to teams, or they approached him regarding Jones’ availability. INDIANAPOLIS – Speculation on which players the Indianapolis Colts are willing to part with as the NFL’s trade deadline nears has included another prominent name. Starting quarterback Daniel Jones. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero posted on social media the Colts have informed inquiring teams “they aren’t trading’’ Jones. Trading Jones would be the latest and brightest flashing sign that owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s reboot for the future has hit full speed. He was signed to a two-year, $88 million contract in March with the express purpose of being the team’s quarterback for at least the short-term. As much as Jones has focused on Sunday’s meeting with Dallas at Lucas Oil Stadium, he admitted he’s heard the trade rumors. “I think just like anything, like any of the other stuff that could come up and distract you from what your job is and your daily preparation, I think getting back to kind of what’s right in front of you and what’s most important right now,’’ he said Wednesday. “The work that we’re doing this week is extremely important for all of us. Coach Shane Steichen has remained supportive of Jones, although that seemed to waver just a bit after the Colts were overwhelmed 42-7 at Jacksonville. Steichen said “every position’’ would be evaluated. Monday he said, “Daniel will be our starting quarterback. I feel that Daniel gives us the best chance to win right now.’’ Initial speculation mentioned the Baltimore Ravens having interest in acquiring Jones. Starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley are on the injured reserve list and No. 3 Joe Fagnano was ineffective in the Ravens’ 33-10 loss to Jacksonville Thursday night. That convinced Baltimore to acquire former Colt Jacoby Brissett in a trade with Arizona this week. Another team that’s been linked to Jones is the Minnesota Vikings, who share the best record in the league at 6-1 but reportedly aren’t satisfied with their quarterback situation. Kyler Murray will miss Monday’s meeting with Buffalo and another former Colt, Carson Wentz, will start against the Bills. Jones spent the final six weeks of the 2024 season on the Vikings’ practice squad after being released by the New York Giants. Minnesota made a strong push to re-sign Jones during the 2025 offseason, but he determined the Colts offered a better opportunity to start and signed a one-year, $14 million deal. If the Vikings were to offer compensation Dodds and Irsay-Gordon couldn’t turn down, they would be acquiring a quarterback mired in arguably the worst season in his eight-year career. New York has wins against the Titans and Browns so far this season. The Jets have lost three straight since that victory over Cleveland. Jets vs. Chiefs Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: I think the Jets are a better team than you think they are at first glance. The Kansas City Chiefs (-9.5) will look to break a two-game losing streak as they host the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, but my Jets vs. Chiefs prediction is all about the Over. New York's defense is struggling even as the team finds more offensive weapons, and that has me backing the points total. Read on to see all my free NFL picks for Sunday, Nov. 8. TOP PICK Jets vs Chiefs prediction: Over 47.5 The New York Jets came into the season expecting to ride their defense to victories, but injuries and a general inability to stop the passing game have exposed that plan. New York has allowed 30.7 ppg over the last three weeks as several key members of the secondary are out of action, and the Jets rank just 19th overall in defensive EPA per play (-0.02) . Patrick Mahomes , Kenneth Walker III , and the rest of the Kansas City Chiefs offense — averaging 23.9 ppg and 6.4 yards per play — will take full advantage of that weakness, but the Jets can score, too. Geno Smith has been very efficient at quarterback, and Braelon Allen has emerged as a weapon in the backfield, with New York scoring 25+ points in back-to-back games . The offenses will dominate on Sunday, and I'm backing the Over at up to 58%. Jets vs Chiefs combo While I think both teams will contribute to a high total in this game, the Chiefs have the clear advantage. New York's offense will be hampered by the likely absence of Garrett Wilson (concussion protocol), and the attempts to reintegrate Breece Hall could slow the attack as well. I like the Chiefs to cover at home. I'm also taking Walker to pick up at least 90 yards on the ground. While the Jets haven't been as bad at stopping the run, they're merely average there, allowing 4.0 yards per carry. Walker is rushing for 110 yards per game this season and should get plenty of carries if and when Kansas City jumps out to an early lead. Kenneth Walker III 90+ rushing yards Jets vs Chiefs touchdown scorer: Rashee Rice While Walker is the easy pick to score for the Chiefs, I see a lot more value in trading on Rashee Rice . The wide receiver has only really played in four games — he was injured in the first quarter of another — but has 20 catches on 24 targets and two scores in that limited time. That alone would give him value, but throw in the fact that he'll be working against a depleted New York secondary, and this is a strong play. I like Rice to score at up to 50%. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 4:57 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their third straight game and sixth of their last seven on Sunday. Last week the Jets lost at home against the previously winless Miami Dolphins. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-6 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Any hopes of a playoff run are all but gone. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City next Sunday. The Chiefs have lost two straight games to tough opponents on the road. This week the Denver Broncos barely survived as the Chiefs were stopped on the one yard line as they were trying for a game winning score as time ran out. The Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a dominant 31 – 10 victory over the Denver Broncos. They followed that impressive win with four straight victories over some of the worst teams in the NFL – the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers. The 5-0 start to the season was great, but with four of the wins coming against bad teams, it is tough to say just how good the Chiefs are. Now they have lost two straight to tough opponents. Are the Chiefs a top team? Maybe. It's not entirely clear. What is crystal clear is the Chiefs are a far, far better team than the Jets. Teams like the Dolphins and the Raiders have snapped their losing streaks against the Jets in East Rutherford. It seems all but inevitable Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will do the same at home. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Chiefs will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 9.5 points. The game has an over/under of 46.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Chiefs are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can at least pull off one of those infamous moral victories and keep the game competitive against a Chiefs team that may understandably have trouble getting up for a game against the hapless Jets. picks.blurb: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football F1 São Paulo GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs with the football and looks to pass during the third quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have beaten the New York Jets in four of their five meetings since 2011, with the most recent being a controversial 23-20 win in 2023. That game saw Michael Carter II's game-clinching interception negated by a phantom penalty on Sauce Gardner and wasted one of the best performances of Zach Wilson's career. In this matchup, the Chiefs will be heavy favorites despite having lost two in a row following a 5-0 start. Let's break down the Chiefs' roster going position by position: The Jets have Patrick Mahomes to reckon with this week, and he's having a solid season as he's posting a quarterback rating of 99.7; his best since 2022. Mahomes has 12 touchdowns and four interceptions and is coming off a good game against the Broncos where he passed for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Behind Mahomes is a familiar face: Jets 2025 starter Justin Fields. Seventh round rookie Garrett Nussmeier is the number three. Offensive Line The Chiefs' interior line is the same as last year led by pro bowlers Creed Humphrey and Trey Smith at center and right guard respectively. Smith has a team-high five offensive penalties. Kingsley Suamataia completes the interior trio at left guard, although he's already been benched twice this year, including on Sunday where he was suddenly replaced before pre-game warmups by Mike Caliendo. That fuelled rumors that was was being disciplined by the coaching staff but Andy Reid denied this. Caliendo, who also started four games last year, has struggled in pass protection. Suamataia is expected to be back in the starting lineup for Sunday's game. The tackle positions have seen some changes as last year's starting right tackle, Jawaan Taylor, was released in March and the starting left tackle – 2025 first round pick Josh Simmons – is on injured reserve. Jaylon Moore, who started a handful of games last year, is currently starting at right tackle, while the left tackle is undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson, who is one of five undrafted rookies on the roster. Moore has given up a team-high three sacks, but Benson – while yet to surrender a sack – has given up the most pressure on the team. Moore missed week seven's game, so former New York Giant Joshua Ezeudu started at right tackle in that one. The other backups are center Hunter Nourzad and another undrafted rookie; tackle Diego Pounds. Running Backs The Chiefs' big offseason acquisition on offense was the reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. The move has been a resounding success as he rushed for 100 yards in four of his first five games as the Chiefs started 5-0. Since then, he's averaged just three yards per carry, though. Even so, he's just 10 yards off the league lead with 770 rushing yards. He has also caught 22 passes. There are two rookies backing up Walker – fifth round pick Emmett Johnson and the undrafted Jaydn Ott. Ott hasn't played yet, though. The Chiefs also have a fullback – Ben VanSumeren – on the roster. However, they will also use defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga in short yardage situations. He has even carried the ball twice. Pass catchers The Chiefs' top pass catching option has once again been tight end Travis Kelce, who has 410 receiving yards to lead the team. The leading pass catcher among the wide receivers is the speedy Xavier Worthy, who has 27 catches, albeit that he's only averaging 8.5 yards per catch. Despite some injury concerns and legal issues, Rashee Rice is now back in the lineup for the Chiefs. He has 20 catches in five games this year. Tyquan Thornton was also starting at wide receiver, but he's now on injured reserve. The backups are Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong, Nikko Remigio and fifth round rookie Cyrus Allen. Royals has seen the most action from this group. At tight end, Noah Gray is a solid contributor who gets plenty of playing time. Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley round out this group. Defensive Line The Chiefs' defensive line is anchored by pro bowler Chris Jones, although he is having a down year statistically with just half a sack, one tackle for loss and three quarterback hits. He had 7.5, 12 and 25 last year. George Karlaftis, who had six sacks last year, has a team-high two sacks and also leads the team with 16 quarterback hits (just one less than the rest of the team combined) and six tackles for loss. Karlaftis also has a team-high with eight passes defensed. In fact, these all eight of these came in the last five games. Prior to that, he had 17 in his first 67 NFL games. Tonga is the other starter at defensive tackle with Felix Anudike-Uzomah the other starting defensive end. Kansas City has been operating a three-man rotation inside with first round rookie Peter Woods getting plenty of playing time. However, Woods has been ruled out with a neck injury so Bryson Eason may need to step up. Last year's second round pick Omarr Norman-Lott remains on the PUP list. The backups on the edge are second round rookie R Mason Thomas and Ashton Gillotte. Undrafted rookie Jack Pyburn is also on the roster. Nick Bolton remains in a full-time role with Drue Tranquill on the field most of the time. Last year, Bolton had 154 tackles and Tranquill added 103. They've been productive this year, too, with Bolton on 68 tackles and Tranquill on 53 tackles, including five tackles for loss. Jack Cochrane gets playing time in three-linebacker sets, while Jeffrey Bassa has seen limited action. Cooper McDonald has yet to play any defensive snaps, though. Defensive Backs The Chiefs suffered a loss a few weeks ago when their top cornerback L'Jairus Sneed was placed on injured reserve. Sneed was also the team's primary slot corner, so they've been using Christian Roland-Wallace in that role for the past few weeks. Nohl Williams and first round rookie Mansoor Delane are the current starters on the outside, although Kristian Fulton started in place of Delane on Sunday. Delane has a shoulder issue which is likely to limit him for the rest of the season but he was expected to return against the Jets. However, he has been ruled out, so Fulton will presumably start again. Melvin Smith and fourth round rookie Jadon Canady are also available to provide depth at cornerback. The starting safeties are Chamarri Conner, who had 117 tackles last season, and offseason signing Alohi Gilman. Jaden Hicks has also been getting playing time in three-safety sets. He also started the first three games with Conner out. Undrafted rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa has played five snaps so far this season. Special Teams Former pro bowl kicker Harrison Butker is having a rough year with six missed field goals already and Justin Tucker waiting in the wings on the practice squad in case he should falter again. Punter Matt Araiza is having his best year statistically in his third season with the Chiefs, though. Remigio is the team's return specialist, although Johnson ends up sharing the work on kickoff returns. Remigio, who is yet to achieve a 50-yard return as he is halfway through his third season, is officially listed as questionable. Bassa and Nwankpa are the team's most productive players in kick coverage this season, but last year they were led by McDonald and Cochrane. Canady and Nwankpa have been the primary gunners.

Dodson · Athlon Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:16 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return home Sunday to face the New York Jets after dropping two straight games. Running back Kenneth Walker III has been bottled up in the defeats after leading the league in rushing through his first five games. The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos limited K9 to a combined 105 rushing yards on 35 carries. Bold Prediction No. 1: Running Back Kenneth Walker Tops 100 Yards The Jets have allowed the seventh-most rushing yards to opposing running backs through eight weeks. Walker topped 100 yards on the ground in four of the first five games of the season. Even after averaging just 3.0 yards per carry the last two games, he's still second in the NFL with 5.5 yards per carry. Two weeks ago, the Jets allowed Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon to rush for 103 yards on 25 carries . Walker is a clear upgrade from Gordon and will gash the Jets on the ground. The Chiefs' passing game has also had its issues. Tight end Travis Kelce has been managing an ankle injury, and they'll look to run the ball often. Bold Prediction No. 2: Chiefs Defense Records 2+ Sacks The Chiefs' pass rush has been much maligned, and it's for good reason. They're tied for last in the NFL with nine sacks on the season. Defensive tackle Chris Jones, who is one of their leading pass rushers, has just a half-sack on the season. Defensive end George Karlaftis reached the quarterback in Week 8 for his team-leading second sack of the season. The Jets are tied for second with 23 sacks allowed on the season. Quarterback Geno Smith has been sacked at least twice in the last seven games. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is known for his relentless blitzing, and the Chiefs will get home two or more times.

away.headline: What Jets Are Saying About Week 9 Injury Report Ahead of Sunday
away.blurb: The good news is that edge rusher David Bailey and running back Breece Hall are both expected to play. Bailey missed Week 8 with a groin injury while a quad injury kept Hall out for the last five. Even better, the team could have their full collection of edge rushers with Joseph Ossai potentially back as well. But with every piece of good news there is also bad. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson has been ruled out for Sunday's contest with a concussion. He reported the injury on Monday and has been in protocol ever since. His absence, coupled with the return of some key veterans, have Jets players and coaches talking about their chances in Week 9 against Kansas City. Here's the full injury report from the Jets' practice on Friday with three clear distinctions on who is out for Sunday: Of note, the three players that are out extend beyond Wilson. Special teamer Trevin Wallace is also out while Ossai, rookie safety VJ Payne, defensive tackle Harrison Phillips, and corner Nahshon Wright are all listed as questionable. The same can be said for the second-overall pick in Bailey. His return gives the team more flexibility to rush the passer—even one as elite as Patrick Mahomes. "He (Bailey) just has to understand that with Mahomes is going to fake throw," Glenn said. "He's going to move around, and we just got to make sure we squeeze the pocket and make sure we don't let him out of the pocket in situations like that." Breaking Down Jets' Injury Report Heading Into Week 9 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chiefs) There is good news and bad news when it comes to the New York Jets injury report heading into Week 9 against the Kansas City Chiefs. The good news is Mason Taylor, Hall, and Bailey are all starters and will need to be on the field for the Jets to have any chance against the Chiefs. Speaking to reporters before practice on Friday, Glenn was clear: the team was prepared to play without Wilson, but that doesn't mean his absence will be anything less than a major blow to the entire unit. "I think it speaks for itself," Glenn said. "Any time you lose a player of that magnitude, it's always tough, right, but we do have other players, and those guys will look forward to the challenge." Glenn did acknowledge the benefit that came from having Hall back in the lineup . He made it clear that the former second-round running back was going to have a role in the offense on Sunday, and it will be to work with rising star Braelon Allen. "I know we're trying to get in this who's going to be the starter and try to spin sort of a negative situation, but nothing's changed from how I see this," Glenn said. "Both of those guys will play and that's just what it is." It's hard to envision a Jets victory on Sunday without Wilson. Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory . Mandatory Credit: Eamon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Erik Schlitt · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 1:15 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they've strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. This season, the Dolphins are focused on improving week to week and laying the foundation for future success. While they sit at 1-6 for the year, they fight each and every week, playing hard until the final whistle, a great sign for a team with 14 rookies and in the midst of a complete franchise rebuild. The Lions come into Sunday's Week 9 game with a 5-2 record and looking like a team that can make a deep run in the NFC playoffs. After a disappointing 9-8 record in 2025 leading to a fourth-place finish in the NFC North, Detroit is looking to return to the form that brought them back-to-back division titles in 2023 and 2024. The NFC North is a tough division, however, with all four teams above the .500 mark and having won at least five times already this season. How will Sunday's game play out? This feels like a game that could get away from the Dolphins, a byproduct of how diametrically opposed their 2026 trajectories are. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook , however, seem to think this game might be a little tighter than might be expected. Phins up! Dive into game day on the SB Nation app!
