Lions (-6.5) at Dolphins Over the last two weeks, I was right on my prediction of the Dolphins beating the Jets straight-up, and on Miami losing to New England but covering the spread. This week, I am not as bullish on the Dolphins' chances. The Lions are the better team in this matchup, and I think they'll cover the 6.5-point spread, even with the injuries they are facing. Miami will play the Lions tough, and they might keep it close for much of the game, but in the end, I think the Lions pull away. Any time touchdown scorer: Ollie Gordon II The Dolphins running game ran into a speedbump against the Patriots. After averaging 125 yards rushing in their last five games, Miami was held to just 74 yards in Week 8. They have to correct that in Week 9. It will not be easy, Detroit has the ninth-ranked rush defense in the league, allowing just 96.6 yards per game. The Dolphins will have to be deliberate in getting the ball to Gordon, continue to feed him even if they are getting stuffed early, and make this a physical game. In the end, I think Gordon will be able to find the endzone at least once in this game and this prop hits. Hockenson, 119 yards; George Kittle, 80 yards; Mason Taylor, 62 yards; Travis Kelce, 59 yards) and would have had five on that list if Hunter Henry had not been injured in the second quarter Patriots game (3 receptions, 30 yards when he departed). Unless Miami comes with a different scheme to handle tight ends, LaPorta reaching 49 yards receiving seems likely. Bell has been targeted more than fellow rookie Caleb Douglas – in part because Douglas missed three games with an injury – but Douglas has one more reception and almost 80 more yards than Bell. Miami is playing it smart with Bell, who tore his ACL less than a year ago, but it has depressed some of his stats this season. The flashes are there, and Miami will need him to flash in this game if they are going to pull off the upset. His longest reception this season was for a 44-yard gain, so the potential for a big play is there. He may not pick up that big of a gain in this game, but a 14-yard reception does not seem out of reach. All odds provides by FanDuel Sportsbook .

Campbell, 26, did not appear to be moving while he was taken off the field, as his teammates looked on with tears and concern. Campbell said Wednesday he is still working on regaining movement in his body, though he does have full movement in his lower body at this time. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” he said in a statement. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger.” Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions lays on the ground after being injured on a play during the fourth quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1. Mike Mulholland via Getty Images “I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” he added. “I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.” Dan Campbell, head coach for the Detroit Lions, previously spoke about visiting Campbell in the hospital, though he declined to share the specifics of his injury or his progress. “I got to go see him last night, it was good, it was positive,” Campbell said during a press conference on Monday. “Got to see his parents, talk to his wife, and everybody’s in good spirits. It’s about the recovery, and it’s a small setback.” Both Lions and Vikings players took a knee on the turf as Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (not pictured) received medical treatment. away.headline: NFL-Lions report positive progress for linebacker Campbell after injury
away.blurb: "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time," the team said in a statement. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

Campbell said the team is preparing to start Scruggs this week, but nothing is finalized. Wonnum is still in the NFL’s concussion protocol, and while he still has a chance to pass the protocols this week, his lack of return to practice suggests he is a bit further back than hoped. Reed said he was in a good spot in his post-game media availability last Sunday, so his absence from practice could mean his injury was worse than he realized or that the team is giving the veteran extra time to be ready. We’ll find out more on Friday. After holding a walkthrough on Wednesday, the Detroit Lions (5-2) returned to the practice field on Thursday as they prepare to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6). While Wednesday’s report was just estimates from the coaching staff, Thursday’s practice mirrored the same level of participation for most players, with a couple of upgrades. With that in mind, here’s Thursday’s injury report and what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . C Cade Mays (ankle) — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start No updates on Campbell since Wednesday . S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 12 Saylors popped up on last week’s injury report with a neck injury and was also forced from the game because of it, but getting in practice reps is a good sign he’s headed in the right direction. St. Brown got a little banged up in Week 7, but it’s rare to see him scale back even a little, so it’s not surprising that he was back on the practice field this week, and expectations are that he is on track to play against the Dolphins. In the locker room on Thursday, St. Brown said he was injured on his non-touchdown catch (the play that was overturned), but added, “I’m a little banged up, but I’ll be alright.” Joseph is expanding his practice exposure this week, but the team is not going to rush him back, and Campbell has already said they don’t plan to activate him this week. He still has 12 days left in his injury evaluation window, which could put him in play for the Lions-Patriots game in Germany, or potentially the following week when they host the Bucs. LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe) – Upgrade from Wednesday S Brian Branch (concussion) – Upgrade from Wednesday Ogbongbemiga did not appear to suffer an injury in Week 7, but he showed up on this week’s injury report with a toe injury. Not much is known about this injury, but getting in a full practice is a good sign he may be able to play on Sunday. If not, the Lions did add two linebackers to the active roster this week and another to the practice squad, in case the team needs more depth. Ya-Sin was added to the injury report with “cramps,” suggesting he required fluids, but there shouldn’t be too much to worry about long term as long as he manages his hydra

(Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kevin Nogle · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions this weekend, hoping to bounce back after a disappointing loss to the New England Patriots last week. Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding a walkthrough rather than a full practice. Jaylen Wright does not practice The Dolphins' second-string running back missed practice with a quadriceps injury. While Wright's contributions on offense have been minimal this year, picking up just 41 yards on 22 carries, he has been strong as a kick returner, where he is averaging 27.6 yards per kick and has a long of 79 yards. Dolphins rookie guard Kadyn Proctor fully participated in Wednesday's practice but remains in the league's concussion protocol, according to head coach Jeff Hafley. "He is progressing in the protocol," Hafley said. Jarrett Kingston, an August waiver claim from the Houston Texans for Miami, started in Proctor's place last week. Good news from Detroit's Jack Campbell The Lions' All-Pro linebacker sustained an ugly injury against the Vikings after tackling tight end T.J. Hockenson. Caught in an awkward position, Campbell hit Hockenson and had his head compress back onto his neck. He fell to the turf and lay motionless before being carted off the field and taken to a hospital. Campbell released a statement on Wednesday, indicating that he is progressing well in his recovery from the injury ( via Pride of Detroit ) : My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive

(Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Chris Pokorny · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns take on the New Orleans Saints this Sunday. The Browns are coming off of a bad loss to the Steelers, but it looks like they'll have a change at quarterback this week (forced by injury) with Shedeur Sanders being under center. The Saints are well-rested, coming off of a bye. Note that some of the picks below were written up before the Browns' quarterback news. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 9 game between the Browns and Saints: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Saints: Shedeur Sanders is in line to start for the Browns with Deshaun Watson, who was playing his best ball since 2020, entering concussion protocol earlier this week. The biggest difference with Sanders under center appears to be his willingness to stretch the field, as his 7.1 air yards per target in 2025 are more than Watson's 6.7 mark through eight games this season. Sanders is also working with a better receivers than he did a year ago with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning big roles in Todd Monken's offense. None of that will ultimately matter if the run game is dormant — as it was last week (34 yards) in Pittsburgh. The Saints' defense has been anything but great against the run, allowing 139.4 rush yards per game (29th in the NFL) and have given up north of 100 yards in all but one game in 2026. But I do see this being a get-right game for the Saints on all fronts fresh off the bye. Changes were made to the run game ( firing run-game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, signing RB Audric Estimé) and the kicking ranks (Charlie Smyth is expected to handle kicking duties after Daniel Carlson's release), and the entire roster got a little healthier. First-round receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice and could be a boon — if he indeed makes his NFL debut — for Tyler Shough opposite Chris Olave. Getting Kelvin Banks Jr. back along an O-line that has struggled to keep Shough clean in the pocket should also benefit Kellen Moore's unit. Sanders can smile all he wants, but the Saints will get the last laugh Sunday. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Saints 17, Browns 14 The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Browns 20, Saints 17 Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Saints 23, Browns 20 The Browns are quickly regressing to the mean and going into a hostile environment to face a hungry, young team after a bye doesn't bode well. New Orleans will have emphasized the need to execute better at home for both Kellen Moore and Brandon Staley. Tyler Shough gets it done, having more reliable weapons than Deshaun Watson. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Saints 20, Browns 17 Both offenses are struggling. Deshaun Watson has taken a league-high 33 sacks, and the Browns average 97.6 rushing yards per game. New Orleans has been worse on the ground, but a bye week comes at the right time. The Saints are 0-4 S/U this season – and this game is a candidate for a walk-off field goal either way. Tyler Shough needs to avoid the interceptions, but New Orleans wins a coin-flip game. Below are our Week 9 NFL staff picks:

Despite their disappointing 2-5 record, the Saints remain just one game out of first place in the NFC South, making Sunday's matchup an important opportunity to gain some ground in the division standings. A victory would not only provide some much-needed momentum but also keep New Orleans firmly in the hunt for the division title as the season enters its second half. For the Saints, Tyler Shough continues to show why he is the future of this franchise despite the team's offensive struggles. Establishing consistency, protecting the football and finding an early rhythm will be key to getting them back in the win column. On the opposite sideline, Shedeur Sanders could get an opportunity to lead the Brown's offense with Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion. They will have to beat the 2-5 New Orleans Saints to do that and hopefully gain some ground in the AFC North. This is a winnable game, and to expect the Browns to win is not a bold opinion. If you want some sort of bold prediction, then we have those too. A forecast that goes beyond that of normal expectations, but also stays in the realm of reality. Here are my three bold predictions for the Browns against the Saints. KC Concepcion rushing score The Saints do not have a good run defense (ranked 29th in rushing yards allowed). I expect the Browns to lean heavily into their running game. This would be especially true if backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders is starting. I expect that Concepcion will be very involved in the passing game. I also think the Browns will look for creative ways to get him touches considering how elusive and explosive he is. Don't be surprised if he finds the end zone on an end-around or a backward pass type play. Judkins goes off I won't go as far as to say that Quinshon Judkins will have his best day of the year because I don't think he outdoes what he did versus the Titans. However, I don't think this game will be way off from that in terms of production. As stated before, the Saints have a bad run defense. It makes sense to take the ball out of the hands of a backup quarterback and run the ball early and often. Look for a 100-yard day and a score from Judkins. Shough-ing turnovers There is no debate that the Browns defense has been their strength this year. They rank 13th in points allowed per game and 13th in total turnovers forced. This pairs with the Browns' advantage, as the Saints are 6th in the NFL in most giveaways. I won't go as far as to predict a turnover fiesta this weekend, but I will predict that Saints Quarterback Tyler Shough has at least two in this game. away.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
away.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. Tyson, the eighth overall pick in this year’s draft, has been out since getting hurt Aug. 13 with a hamstring injury and missed the Saints’ first seven games, but he returned to practice this week. Most of the team’s struggles have centered around the run game — the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti on Monday — but Tyson provides another dynamic weapon in the passing game, which could help open up New Orleans’ rushing attack. The Saints had previously listed Tyson as questionable. home.headline: The Saints make a decision on rookie WR Jordyn Tyson’s status ahead of Browns game
home.blurb: The New Orleans Saints plan to activate the rookie wide receiver off injured reserve for Sunday’s game against the Cleveland Browns, according to a report. Tyson, the eighth overall pick in this year’s draft, has been out since getting hurt Aug. 13 with a hamstring injury and missed the Saints’ first seven games, but he returned to practice this week. Tyson’s return should help a Saints offense that has been uneven this season. The Saints rank 14th in points per game, but 23rd in total offense. Most of the team’s struggles have centered around the run game — the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti on Monday — but Tyson provides another dynamic weapon in the passing game, which could help open up New Orleans’ rushing attack. The Saints had previously listed Tyson as questionable. NFL insider Jordan Schultz first reported the news. The Saints, too, had been patient with Tyson since drafting him. Though draft analysts were concerned about the receiver’s durability due to Tyson’s injury history in college, the Saints were confident that Tyson would be able to hold up in the NFL. They slow-played his reps in the spring as he recovered from a separate hamstring injury, and when Tyson got hurt again this summer, the Saints avoided setting a firm timeline for his recovery. Tyson, speaking to reporters Wednesday, said his hamstring now feels 100% and that he even feels “more explosive” after the injury. home.headline: Saints finally get good injury news on Jordyn Tyson amid lengthy IR stint
home.blurb: While they might not be out of the divisional race just yet, the Saints really need things to turn around soon, or else this season will end in disappointment. Fortunately, during their bye week, the Saints got some great news on a key injured player. "Saints first-pick Jordyn Tyson could return from the hamstring injury that has sidelined him as early as next week vs. the Browns , per sources," Schefter reports. "But even if it's not then, he is not far away from playing." Rushing him back before the bye would've made no sense, especially for a team that's likely still trying to climb out of the bottom of the NFC. But now, Tyson is closing in on a return to action, which would make for his NFL debut the moment he's active and steps on the field for New Orleans. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense Michael Owens/Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. home.headline: New York Giants not underestimating injured Eagles RB Saquon Barkley
home.blurb: The Giants can't let the Eagles' woes concern them. Barkley has been limited in practice this week, but he will play Sunday, and as we know, if Barkley is suited up, he's potentially a dangerous customer. “I’m expecting [Barkley] to be healthier than he has been so far,” defensive lineman Shelby Harris told the New York Post this week . “They’ve done a good job trying to manage him on his way back from injury. If he’s going to play, I expect to get the best out of him — full-on star Saquon Barkley. And we’ll have to stop him in order to be successful.” "Oh, he’s an elusive dude, man," Harbaugh told reporters this week. "I mean, they're one of the league leaders in making tacklers miss. I'm pretty sure he's a big part of that, and that's just what he does. So, he can take the ball from the A-gap to the edge, to the backside edge, like that. That's what he does. He's still doing it. He's a threat catching the ball out of the backfield, checkdowns, things like that. So, all hands on deck. All hands on deck when he's out there." home.blurb: Skattebo and Carter officially did not practice. These notable players were limited participants, though all figure to play Sunday: right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), cornerback Colton Hood (illness), returner Charlie Jones (hand) and left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin). Skattebo hurt his hamstring during overtime of the Giants’ thrilling pre-bye week win in Houston. He downplayed the injury after the game. But clearly, it is a lingering problem, even coming out of the bye. With Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve and out for at least the next four games, the Giants on Sunday might need to turn to Devin Singletary as their primary back. Carter was not on the injury report at all leading up to the Houston game. But a game prior, he was listed as questionable to face the Saints because of a calf issue. Carter did not practice Wednesday or Thursday that week — and then was limited on Friday. He wound up playing 65% of the snaps against New Orleans. home.headline: Eagles' QB Joe Milton Talks Preparation Ahead of 1st NFL Start vs. Giants Amid Jalen Hurts Injury
home.blurb: Joe Milton III will make his first NFL start on Sunday against the New York Giants as the floundering Philadelphia Eagles try to end a six-game losing streak. For Milton, staying ready for such a moment was a key part of his preparations throughout the season. "You never know what can happen in NFL. That's kind of how I took it. Yes, I was on the practice squad, and I was just preparing for any moment that presents itself," he told reporters . "Still, when I was at Dallas on the practice squad, I was just pretty much going through the plays, going through the week like I was a starter or like I was playing, and just being ready. And that's what the NFL is about: Just being ready when your name is called and just preparing for those moments. And I've been preparing and still preparing for the week." Milton will be the fourth quarterback Philly has used this season behind starter Jalen Hurts and backups Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee. But while those quarterbacks were with the team during training camp, the Birds signed Milton off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad in mid-October. And now it's his moment in the spotlight. According to Stick to the Model's injury tracker through Week 8, the Rams have lost $37 million in player value due to injuries, the third-highest total in the NFL. Only the Packers ($42.1 million) and Patriots ($40.3 million) have lost more. The tracker calculates the value lost when a starter misses a game, with each absence costing 1/17 of what that player's grade earns at his position. Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua have accounted for two of the Rams' biggest losses, according to Stick to the Model. Garrett has missed seven games due to a knee injury, while Nacua missed two games earlier this year with a groin injury. Cornerback Trent McDuffie also missed Weeks 6 and 7 with a groin injury. Fortunately, Garrett is at least getting closer to returning from injured reserve after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Interestingly, the Rams haven't lost nearly as many games from their starters as some other teams. They've had 28 starter games missed due to injury or illness, just above the league average of 25.5 and tied for 12th-most. That makes their third-place standing in player value lost particularly notable. The Rams haven't necessarily had the most absences, but the players they've lost have carried significant value. With Watson now joining the list of season-altering injuries, Los Angeles will have to continue finding ways to overcome the attrition as it pushes through the second half of the season. away.headline: Los Angeles Rams Get Encouraging Matthew Stafford Injury Update
away.blurb: Written by NDTV Sports Desk Updated: November 05, 2026, 7:53 AM EST Read Time: 2 min facebook twitter WhatsApp reddit E-mail Matthew Stafford during an NFL game. © X/@RamsNFL The Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford walking around with ice wrapped around his throwing elbow raises questions about his health. With the team already dealing with several injuries, losing another player was the last thing they needed. However, Stafford had a rather relaxed response when reporters asked about his condition on Wednesday, November 4. The 38-year-old made it clear that the soreness had not affected his work or his ability to play. Matthew Stafford speaks out on injury concern Stafford did not appear particularly concerned about the attention surrounding his elbow. In fact, he joked that reporters had only recently started noticing something he had been doing throughout the season. "You guys have been blind. I feel like I've been icing my arm every day out here, walking around," the quarterback told reporters. He then explained that some discomfort was understandable at this stage of his career. Stafford, in his 18th NFL season, admitted the physical demands of competing against younger players but insisted that the issue had not stopped him from practicing or taking snaps on game day. "Listen, I'm 38 years old, trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year," he added. His comments gave some relief after head coach Sean McVay had confirmed earlier in the week that Stafford was experiencing soreness in his right arm. The quarterback had been spotted with ice on his elbow after the 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8. The first injury report for Week 9 listed Stafford with a right elbow issue, but he remained a full participant in practice. That was another positive sign for a team relying heavily on its veteran quarterback. Los Angeles Rams face a growing injury list Stafford's update came at a time when the Los Angeles Rams had several other players dealing with injuries. Cornerback Jaylen Watson became the latest major loss after suffering a shoulder injury that required season-ending surgery. He was the third Rams player to suffer a season-ending injury in two weeks. Wide receiver Davante Adams was among those missing from the team's first Week 9 practice report, while cornerback Trent McDuffie was listed with a back injury. Tight end Colby Parkinson remained sidelined with the rib injury that kept him out against the Los Angeles Chargers. Stafford admitted that every NFL season brought its own challenges and said he did not spend time comparing the current situation with previous injury-hit campaigns. He said that players in the training room were working hard to return, adding that their availability would give the team a good welcome . away.headline: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest on Rams Star's Status vs. Commanders
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. The 30-year-old veteran set the single-season NFL sack record in 2025 with 23, and the Rams likely assumed they would get something resembling that level of production out of him. Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Garrett is expected to play on Sunday after NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Garrett was "on track to be activated" after practicing all week. Garrett was activated off of injured reserve on Saturday after he did not have a designation on the team's injury report Friday. Garrett has not played since Week 1, as he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve following the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. L.A. made the blockbuster trade of the offseason when it acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for pass-rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, and 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Garrett was coming off the best season of his career. However, Garrett did not look himself in Week 1 after battling a knee injury during training camp and the preseason, and the decision was made for him to undergo surgery and heal up. Given that the Rams entered the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites, the 2026 campaign has been largely disappointing thus far. Los Angeles has a 4-4 record, placing it third in the NFC West, and it would not be a playoff team if the season ended today. Garrett could give the defense a significant lift if he is fully healthy and back to his usual form, though, which is ideal with winnable games on tap against the Commanders and Arizona Cardinals the next two week. The schedule gets tougher after that with games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and 49ers, and the Rams' likely hope by that point is that Garrett will have knocked off the rust and be positioned to contribute in a major way.

Rams without Treylon Burks or Dyami Brown, the team announced Friday evening on its official injury report. Burks is dealing with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. Brown suffered a calf injury in Thursday’s practice that the Commanders are concerned about. Johnny Newton was considered questionable on the injury report, as those on IR with open practice windows usually are. We should learn about his availability on Saturday. TE John Bates – Limited all week with a shoulder injury All this comes shortly after Terry McLaurin was lost for the year with a torn petellar tendon in his knee. As The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala originally pointed, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams were the only receivers at practice who have caught a pass in a game to this point. That’s, well, not great. The injury report was relatively clean outside of that, though the team has absorbed significant recent losses of those — like Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols — who are now on injured reserve. Also, NFL Network reports that superstar Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett is expected to be activated off injured reserve for Sunday’s game. Here’s the full Commanders injury report: WR Dyami Brown – Suffered calf injury during Thursday’s practice WR Treylon Burks – Suffered foot injury vs 49ers DT Jer’Zhan Newton – 21-day practice window opened; returning from IR (pec) DL Shy Tuttle – Has a shoulder issue from Week 8 G Sam Cosmi – Dealing with a new knee injury, full practice Friday OT Josh Conerly – Dealing with a new finger issue QB Jayden Daniels – Still listed with Week 2 elbow dislocation TE Colson Yankoff – New knee injury What’s your level of concern with the state of the Commanders injury situation? home.headline: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest on Rams Star's Status vs. Commanders
home.blurb: Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. The 30-year-old veteran set the single-season NFL sack record in 2025 with 23, and the Rams likely assumed they would get something resembling that level of production out of him. Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Garrett is expected to play on Sunday after NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Garrett was "on track to be activated" after practicing all week. Garrett was activated off of injured reserve on Saturday after he did not have a designation on the team's injury report Friday. Garrett has not played since Week 1, as he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve following the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. L.A. made the blockbuster trade of the offseason when it acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for pass-rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, and 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Garrett was coming off the best season of his career. However, Garrett did not look himself in Week 1 after battling a knee injury during training camp and the preseason, and the decision was made for him to undergo surgery and heal up. Given that the Rams entered the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites, the 2026 campaign has been largely disappointing thus far. Los Angeles has a 4-4 record, placing it third in the NFC West, and it would not be a playoff team if the season ended today. Garrett could give the defense a significant lift if he is fully healthy and back to his usual form, though, which is ideal with winnable games on tap against the Commanders and Arizona Cardinals the next two week. The schedule gets tougher after that with games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and 49ers, and the Rams' likely hope by that point is that Garrett will have knocked off the rust and be positioned to contribute in a major way.

home.blurb: After consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons for Washington in 1978 and 1979, Riggins, who greeted Gibbs with a beer in each hand, sat out the 1980 season over a contract dispute. The Redskins went 6-10 without him. The first thing you notice is the arm. Milton can rifle short and intermediate throws without needing a big wind-up or much of a step into the ball. It almost looks like a flick of the wrist, and the ball arrives with unusual zip. The release is quick, too. He does not need a long gathering motion to generate velocity, which matters when a defender is closing or when the offense wants the ball out before the underneath coverage can rally. That quick release could also make the Eagles’ RPO game more dangerous. A bubble or slant has to get out before the defender responsible for the receiver can drive downhill. Milton has the arm to deliver those throws quickly, and the ball can arrive before the defense has time to recover. The speed of the delivery gives the concept a chance to punish a defense for overcommitting to the run. Receivers may need to adjust, because the ball comes in hot, but this is a rare physical tool. It jumps out on film. The same velocity that makes an RPO throw difficult to defend can also make an ordinary catch harder if the ball is high or behind the receiver. home.headline: 3 biggest storylines for the Rams on Sunday vs. Commanders
home.blurb: How will he look? Is he truly ready to return? How will his return impact the rotation? Garrett could change Los Angeles' fortunes for the better, but what that will look like remains to be seen. Also, as much as we hate to ask, is his body ready for the upcoming part of the season? The Rams' championship hopes are likely riding on it. Despite Kyren Williams and Blake Corum's big-time performance against the Las Vegas Raiders two weeks ago, head coach Sean McVay abandoned the run – especially out of multiple tight end formations – for a pass-happy approach out of 11 personnel last Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. That was the plan of attack in the first half, with the offense going nowhere until they turned up the tempo to close out the half. McVay went to the power run in the second half; Corum had himself a day before Williams closed the game out. With Jaylen Watson out for the season, we're about to witness exactly how strong this defensive secondary really is, while we have to wait and see what the offense has in store. The major storyline revolves around special teams. Through eight games, the Rams have yet to field a competent unit. No big names are walking through the door, so do they have enough to win a championship? The Los Angeles Rams travel to visit the Washington Commanders this week, hoping to come away with a victory and a winning record for the first time this season. Here are the major storylines entering the contest. On Friday, the Rams declared that star defender Myles Garrett will play for the first time since Week 1. After undergoing surgery following the team's loss in Australia, Garrett has yet to play for the franchise in the United States. Now, he will do so in Landover, Maryland. Will McVay trust the sword over the pen? Will McVay wait once again to get his running backs going, or will he finally switch up his style, trusting his Jimmys and Joes over Xs and Os? The Rams have yet to make a trade and likely won't before the November 10th trade deadline. They haven't been major buyers during the middle of the season since their acquisition of Von Miller in 2021, so this Washington game will serve as the final preview of what the roster will look like down the stretch. The Broncos must guard against the "trap-game" nature of this matchup and handle the Panthers on the road. It's an East Coast road game with an early start, which has traditionally been an obstacle for the Broncos, but not since Sean Payton became the head coach in 2023. The Broncos have turned that particular ship around. The Panthers have some young playmakers on offense and a defense that's better than some people realize. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. home.headline: Panthers Sign Jakorian Bennett As Cornerback Depth Crumbles
home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are scrambling to find bodies for the secondary, and they finally found one on Friday. After working out with the staff on Thursday, Jakorian Bennett, the former Las Vegas Raiders fourth-round pick, was signed to the practice squad by the team. Bennett's practice squad signing comes after he cleared waivers unclaimed, leaving the 26-year-old cornerback available for a team in desperate need of help. To make room for this new addition, the Panthers released practice squad member Zion Childress, swapping one depth piece for another in a frantic effort to stabilize a broken back end. The team is already without Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, and Akayleb Evans due to various injuries. Rookie Will Lee III has been sidelined all week with a hamstring issue and is likely to be ruled out of the upcoming matchup. Consequently, only Chau Smith-Wade and Malcolm DeWalt IV remain on the active roster as healthy corners prepared to play. Per Sporting News , the pass defense struggled significantly against the Green Bay Packers in the recent 27-19 loss, and the injury list is the primary reason for that breakdown. Despite the thin depth chart, interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash is refusing to panic. "Obviously, we're down a couple of guys, but I have faith in who we have," interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash said. He also highlighted the specific value of practice squad callup Marco Wilson, who played 69 defensive snaps last week and performed well. "I like where we're at and (Marco Wilson's) got a certain skill set where I think we can get something out of him," Wash added. The clock is ticking, but the Panthers can simply trade for a solution. With the November 10 trade deadline approaching, head coach Dave Canales admits the options are limited. The team simply cannot trade for anyone to fix the immediate hole, forcing them to rely on internal moves and tryouts. "That's all stuff we have to consider," head coach Dave Canales said regarding the constraints. home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers will enter Sunday’s home game against the Denver Broncos without the four cornerbacks who had formed their top layer of depth this season. Rookie cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring) was ruled out Friday, while cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad), Mike Jackson (groin) and Akayleb Evans (knee) remain on injured reserve. That leaves Carolina with active-roster cornerback Chau Smith-Wade and a thin group of other available options as interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash prepares for his first game calling the defense. Horn and Jackson were Carolina’s starting pair before their September injuries. Evans started three games, and Lee had taken on a larger role. Locked On Panthers host Julian Council said the Panthers are likely to lean on practice squad cornerbacks Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton alongside Smith-Wade. Council projected Wilson and Thornton as the outside starters, though Carolina must make any required game-day elevations before that alignment becomes official. Thornton has not appeared in a regular-season game since breaking his leg against the San Francisco 49ers last season. The depleted secondary puts more pressure on a defense already adjusting to a coaching change. Panthers head coach Dave Canales promoted Wash from defensive line coach after Ejiro Evero was fired Oct. 30. Council said the biggest unanswered question is whether Wash will make any front or coverage adjustments while trying to stabilize a unit that now has little margin for another injury at cornerback. Carolina’s immediate task is finding enough workable coverage combinations to get through the Broncos matchup. Smith-Wade’s ability to move between nickel and outside roles, along with whatever the Panthers get from Wilson and Thornton, will shape how much flexibility Wash has in his debut. picks.blurb: Chargers-Texans Game Preview: Can 2 returning starters on offense make the difference? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football F1 São Paulo GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (83) limps off the field during the NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Michael Peterson · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:35 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chargers are back inside SoFi Stadium to face the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. It's been hell for Justin Herbert and the offense all year, but it's been just as rough when they've played the Texans each of the past two seasons. Houston has picked off Herbert five times and chances are they'll add to that total this weekend given how things have gone for two months of the season now. Can they FINALLY shock the fan base and dig out their first win? Will the woes continue against Houston? I guess we have to tune in to find out. Here are the three things I'll be watching the closest when these two teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) How will the Chargers offense look with reinforcements en route? The Chargers offense will hopefully look a bit different this week with a pair starters returning to the fold. Tight end David Njoku had his activation window opened this week and has logged a pair of limited practices this week. He was one of Justin Herbert's top targets through the team's first two games and I'll be interested to see if that continues once he's back. Kayode Awosika, the team's starting left guard to begin the season, also looks to be making his way back to the field after a pair of limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Awosika was one of the offensive line's best performance before going down with a fibula injury and I wouldn't be shocked if his presence next to Joe Alt on the left side moves the needle — in some way at least — on offense this week. Njoky being a pass-catching tight end first and forement could help the passing game while Awosika's return could potentially open up things on the ground. Now of course one player in each facet likely isn't enough to be a true fix, but that unit needs anything at all and two former starters returning to the field is a good start. 2.)Will the nightmare continue for Justin Herbert against the Texans? The last two times Justin Herbert and the Chargers have faced the Texans have been a nightmare. In last year's matchup on December 25th, the Chargers lost 20-16 in a game Herbert threw one touchdown to one interception. The prior game against Houston was the wild card matchup in January of '25 where Herbert threw four interceptions in one of his worst outings as a pro. As much as I wish I could say this is a real opportunity to exorcise the demons from those two games, I simply cannot. Herbert and the Chargers have never looked like a worse, less-cohesive unit and even with the Houston defense not its usual elite self, they still have numerous players who can make a splash play at a moment's notice. Even the return of a healthy Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Tre' Harris did next to nothing for the offense's production in Week Eight. Coming out of the bye, the Chargers scored just nine points, all of which came in the first half. They were then completely blanked in the second as Herbert threw his second interception on top of nearly losing a fumble that was luckily knocked out of bounds. At this rate, nothing is going to come to save the Chargers from themselves. If they want the nightmare to end, they've gotta wake up and do it themselves. 3.) Chargers pass defense will have another tough task vs. WR Nico Collins and a rejuvenated C.J. Stroud Stroud did not have to play at an All-Pro or Pro Bowl level the past two seasons while the Texans defense was arguably the best in the league from 2024-2025. This year, with the defense taking some steps back, he's had to carry the load a bit more and that's somewhat worked out after a rough start. The Texans are the NFL's 7th-ranked passing offense and that is mainly due to an abysmal run game averaging only 84.7 yards per game (29th). After throwing for at least 260 yards in Weeks Four through Six (including two games of over 300), Stroud only threw for 153 in their loss to the Giants just before their bye. With two weeks of preparation, you have to think they'll be ready to roll. On the flip side, the Chargers pass defense currently ranks 7th in the league, as well (198.4). That rank has mostly been maintained without All-Pro safety Derwin James or veteran cornerback Donte Jackson in the lineup. If that's not the far-and-away strength of the Bolts defense, then I don't know what is. Just a bunch of names putting together a top-10 unit under a first-year defensive coordinator. Will that be enough this week?

home.headline: Chargers final injury report before NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and continue to shock the NFL world by showing an unwillingness to trade any of their players despite facing down a lost season in 2026. Los Angeles had hoped to right the ship and gain some momentum coming out of their week seven bye but looked listless against the Los Angeles Rams in week eight. The Chargers do have other players who may be targets on the trade market but so far the word that has been put out to insiders around the NFL is that the Chargers are continuing to execute their plan of standing pat and trying to right the ship before heading into the 2027 season. The return of Donte Jackson to field is intriguing as he has been floated as a possible trade candidate and the Chargers have built up significant young depth both on the roster and the practice squad. The Chargers have been battered by injuries this season. The joke around the NFL may be about the San Francisco 49ers electrical substation and its proximity to the practice facility but someone may need to look into the water in Los Angeles with the amount of injuries both LA teams have faced this season. By week six, the Chargers had over half of their original 53-man roster either on that week's injury report or on injured reserve. The Chargers are already down to their fifth option at left guard and despite hope for getting reinforcements to face the Houston Texans, it appears guard Kayode Awosika, who has not played since week two, is still at least one week away from returning to the field. The Chargers opened the practice windows for tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman this week but it appears that neither are ready to be activated off of injured reserve just yet. The Chargers are set to get some depth at cornerback returning to the field with Donte Jackson and rookie Rodney Shelley clear of the injury report and will carry no injury designation into the game on Sunday. The Chargers front office has been shockingly unwilling to engage with trade calls despite their record generating buzz and demand . The most obvious trade candidate, edge rusher Khalil Mack, has publicly stated that he wants to stay and head coach Jim Harbaugh has echoed that sentiment at the podium. Whether Mack is simply being a consummate professional or he really does not want to uproot and leave his family behind remains to be seen with the trade deadline just days away. If the Chargers lose to the Texans, drop to 0-8 and maintain they are not willing to trade anyone, they might no longer be operating under logic and may be relying on the force. Los Angeles is starting to get some of their injured players back and perhaps, the front office and ownership feel getting the team somewhat stable during the back half of the season and heading into the offseason is more important than a few day three draft picks. home.blurb: Al-Shaair has been working his way back from a lingering groin injury that kept him out for Week 4's game against the Dallas Cowboys. Now, after continuing to get back to 100% from said groin issue, it seems like he's all set to play on Sunday. As for Pitre, his return to the lineup is due for a bit more attention. Pitre has been sidelined for the Texans since suffering an AC joint sprain in his shoulder against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. David Montgomery Remains Out for Sunday Head coach DeMeco Ryans made it clear on Wednesday that David Montgomery will be missing his third-straight game this weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers. And on Thursday, he logged his second DNP of the week . Another starter who's been missing time for the Texans–– but on the defensive side of the ball–– is safety Reed Blankenship, who's missed his fifth-straight practice as a DNP, and is trending towards being out against Los Angeles for Week 9 . If Blankenship was just dealing with concussion protocol, there's a chance that if he is able to practice in limited capacity on Friday and clear protocol within 24 hours. But Blankenship is also dealing with a hand issue that might be making his return to play more complicated. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 9 Upset Pick Minnesota Vikings (+150) vs. Buffalo Bills Josh Allen has a history of struggling against defenses as aggressive as the one Brian Flores operates. Allen did finally get by the Texans in Week 1, but that defense has drastically regressed this season. The Vikings’ defense has formed into what many expected to see out of the Texans in 2026. Minnesota is No. 1 in points allowed (13.3) and No. 2 in total defense (271.6). Yes, I do worry about Minnesota’s poor offense, but maybe Kyler Murray turns it around against the Bills’ poor defense, which is allowing 25.9 points per game. This will come down to Allen against the Vikings’ vaunted defense. Peter Dewey Week 9 Upset Pick Green Bay Packers (+140) vs. New England Patriots The Green Bay Packers can’t run the ball this season, averaging just 2.9 yards per carry, but that may not matter on the road against the New England Patriots in Week 9. New England is 20th in the league in EPA/Pass and eighth in EPA/Rush on defense, so the Packers and Jordan Love are likely going to lean on their elite passing game on Sunday. The Pack are coming off a mini-bye after playing on Thursday against Carolina, and they’ve won four of their last five games after a 1-2 start. Meanwhile, New England is extremely banged up at receiver and was in a dogfight against the lowly Miami Dolphins in Week 8 before pulling away in the second half. The Pats have struggled a bit against elite competition this season, losing to Seattle, Jacksonville, and Chicago. Will we see a similar result against Green Bay? The Packers are quietly fifth in the NFL in EPA/Play on defense, and Love has been playing at a high level all season long. There aren’t a ton of great upset spots this week, but Green Bay’s recent form is intriguing against a banged-up New England squad. Iain MacMillan Week 9 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+240) vs. Chicago Bears You can win a lot of games in the National Football League if you can run the ball effectively and play elite defense, and that's exactly what the Buccaneers have been doing. In fact, they shut the Falcons out last week without completing a single pass. They now enter this week ranked inside the top seven in every rushing metric, second in opponent EPA per play, and third in opponent success rate. We don't currently know what sort of form Baker Mayfield is in, but if he's in peak form when the Bucs need him to take to the air, Tampa Bay is going to be an extremely dangerous team. I have little bad to say about the Bears, who have proven me wrong about my preseason evaluation of them. Drake Maye and Jordan Love have been some of the best passers in the NFL this season and their Sunday matchup should be a good one. Even though the Packers are sitting in the basement of the NFC North, this game will be a good measuring stick for the Patriots as they look to remain in contention for the top spot in the AFC East. Ahead of Week 9, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right? Hurwitz: Make Things Difficult For Jordan Love New England Patriots linebacker Josh Uche (55) and Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) dive for a fumbled snap during their preseason football game Saturday, August 19, 2023, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Love has been playing really well this season , especially when it comes to uncorking it and launching it deep.
