picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions on Why Packers Will Beat Patriots Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have their eyes on the Super Bowl. So do the New England Patriots, who lost in last year’s Super Bowl. On Sunday, these storied teams will collide in Foxborough. The Patriots are three-point favorites. With Tom Brady on the call and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame, here are three reasons why the Packers will spoil the party and earn a statement win. 1. Depleted Patriots Offense The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year despite the lack of a legit threat at receiver. So, they attempted to rectify that problem by signing Romeo Doubs, who had a solid four seasons with the Packers, and trading for A.J. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowler who had surpassed 1,000 yards in six of his first seven seasons. Neither player will be on the field for this game, though. Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and Brown is out again with a knee injury. Combined with the questionable status of top tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, the Packers’ strong defense will face a diluted New England attack. Without Brown and Doubs and with Henry limited to eight snaps with an injured foot, the Patriots needed to rally past the lowly Dolphins last week. The Patriots were held to merely 313 yards. The key for the Packers will be limiting the Rhamondre Stevenson-led running game and putting the pressure on New England’s passing game to make plays against a Packers defense that ranks fourth in opponent passer rating. “I think first of all, he’s an elite quarterback in the pocket, out of the pocket,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said of Drake Maye. “He’s extremely dangerous. He can make any throw. Obviously, he’s super-smart. “They got a great offensive coordinator, great receivers, great playmakers around him and, obviously, when the run game’s going they can do everything and they can throw it just as good as they can run it. So, we’re going to have our hands full for sure and got to make sure that we’re ready to play.” Prediction: The Patriots are going to have a hard time stringing together sustained success on offense. 2. Drake Maye May Screw Up Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is one of the best in the business. He was one vote away from winning NFL MVP last year. However, unless you’re one of the undisputed elite quarterbacks, a quarterback oftentimes is only as good as his supporting cast. So, while Maye is seventh in completion percentage, third in yards per attempt and fifth in touchdowns, only three quarterbacks have thrown more than Maye’s eight interceptions and his six fumbles are one off the unwelcome NFL lead. “I think speaking from playing zone coverage, they’ve got great eyes,” Maye told reporters this week. “They got eyes on the quarterback, they make plays on the football. They can, obviously, catch well. The safeties are great players. They do a lot of things well and they read the quarterback very well, mix up in zone looks. Tip balls have turned into picks that they’ve shown. “So, they’ve just had a habit of creating turnovers in the pocket with the quarterback. They have got some free rushers’ help, too, of the quarterback panicking and trying to fit some stuff to tight windows. They’re good at keeping you in some negative plays. They make you go longer distances. It’s hard.” In the Patriots’ three losses, Maye has thrown three touchdowns vs. six interceptions. In the five wins, it’s 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. His eight interceptions equal last year’s total (in less than half the attempts) are only two off his total from his rookie season in 2024. Prediction: It only takes one big mistake to swing a game between equal teams. Based on this season, Maye is more apt to make that mistake. 3. Turnovers (And Taking Advantage of Them) “The ball” is the most important thing in the sport, coach Matt LaFleur likes to say. Teams that take away and protect the ball tend to win; teams that don’t tend to lose. The Packers are tied for fourth in the league at plus-4 in turnovers. After creating only 14 takeaways last season – when Micah Parsons was on the field for 14 games – they rank second in the league with 15 takeaways this season. The Patriots this year are minus-7 overall; only the white-flag-of-surrender-waving Colts are worse at minus-11. Their 15 giveaways are the third-most in the league. Added together, you get this chart. Points Off Turnovers through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/UmVq9xw7uU The Packers are third in the league by scoring 52 points off takeaways; the Patriots are tied for 23rd with 20 points off takeaways. Green Bay’s aggressive, playmaking defense works hand-in-hand with quarterback Jordan Love’s aggressive, playmaking approach to the position. “Nobody’s had more 20-yard pass plays,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. “(Love is) a quarterback that’s wildly efficient. He has a few off-days, but they’re few and far between. They throw shots. They’ve, obviously, great speed on the edges. They have an excellent tight end, Tucker Kraft, and now getting [Josh] Jacobs back, it seems like they’re trying to work him back in there a little bit more and see what he can do for them in the red zone and things like that. I think they’ve protected better the last few games. “I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that’s an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he’s able to find [Matthew] Golden, [Christian] Watson or Tucker Kraft. Defensively, very physical. They have the second-most negative plays and created the second-most negative plays in the league. Seventeen percent of their drives end in a turnover, so that leads the league, as well.” Love is cooking. He and Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with at least two touchdown passes in seven games this season. “Our goal every week is to go 1-0, and this is a very good team,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, they were in the Super Bowl last year for a reason. They’re very good in, really, all three phases. They got an elite defense. I think they do a lot of things really well. They got two really good corners on the outside. “Yeah, I got a lot of respect for them. It’s always a good test, but I think the goal for us to see how we can go out there and execute the plan, and the goal is to come away victorious. We know to put ourselves in the best position late in the season. We got to really just win every game, and that’s the mindset of going 1-0 every week. It’ll be a good test for us.” Prediction: The Packers have at least two takeaways in five consecutive games. If they can do it again, they’ll win. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. away.headline: Packers make 2 updates to week 9 injury report: Keisean Nixon DNP
away.blurb: Nixon did not practice on Thursday while dealing with a groin injury. He was listed as limited on Wednesday. The veteran has not missed a game since signing with the Packers before the 2022 season, but he might need to practice Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the New England Patriots. Lloyd, who suffered through two injury-plagued seasons to start his NFL career, has his first injury of 2026: a knee injury. He was limited on Thursday. It's possible the Packers could return Chris Brooks this week, providing depth at running back if Lloyd can't go. Micah Parsons practiced in a limited capacity for the second straight day after returning on Wednesday. The Packers were in pads on Thursday. Parsons is not expected to play until Week 12 at the earliest. away.blurb: Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins is set to return to practice, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport reported on Wednesday. Hollins has missed the last four games after being placed on the injured reserved list with a calf injury. A return to practice opens a 21-day window for Hollins to be activated, but he could also make his return as soon as Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The New England Patriots may be getting much-needed reinforcements for their injury-depleted receiving corps. Hollins reeled in 15 catches for 209 yards through four games prior to his injury, but his value to the team goes beyond his statistical production. The 33-year-old wide receiver has excelled as a blocker on running plays and has been a steady veteran presence in the locker room. Brown and Romeo Doubs headlined the Patriots' offseason acquisitions, but both players have missed significant time due to injuries. New England also parted ways with wide receivers Stefon Diggs and Kayshon Boutte, who led the team in yards and touchdowns last season, respectively. The Patriots are entering one of the toughest stretches on their schedule, and Hollins would immediately bolster a wide receiver room that dwindled down to just DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III last week. away.headline: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report
away.blurb: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Keisean Nixon, two running backs questionable for Sunday Emma Pravecek, packers.com CB Keisean Nixon GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and running backs MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and Chris Brooks (ankle) as questionable for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. "It's always concerning when a guy doesn't practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur on Friday morning. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. Rhyan hasn't practiced since injuring his ankle four snaps into the Packers' Week 7 game in Detroit. Receiver Christian Watson (ribs), guard Aaron Banks (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (personal) didn't receive game statuses and will be available Sunday. Watson broke a rib during the Packers' 27-19 win over Carolina but returned to finish the game. He wore protective padding while practicing in a limited capacity this week. New England has ruled out receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and listed seven question: tight end Hunter Henry (foot), cornerback Carlton Davis (neck), safety Kevin Byard (chest), receiver Mack Hollins (calf/injured reserve), tackle Morgan Moses (foot), safety Brenden Schooler (hamstring) and guard Greg Van Roten (hamstring/IR). The Patriots didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder), cornerback Marcus Jones (foot), defensive tackle Christian Barmore (illness), and linebackers Gabe Jacas (knee) and Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder/knee). ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window **Designated for Return from Reserve List/Injured CB Keisean Nixon has been added to the injury report and is questionable for tonight's game against the Panthers news Packers list four questionable, rule out three vs. Panthers | Week 8 Injury Report WR Matthew Golden, DT Devonte Wyatt questionable for Thursday night news Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report news Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Wes Hodkiewicz packers.c

away.blurb: Packers-Patriots Final Injury Report: Keisean Nixon Provides Fun Clue; Five Out Skip to main content SI.COM GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon is questionable for Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. Not all questionable designations are created equal, and Nixon’s jovial conversation with reporters after practice on Friday strongly suggests he will be on the field against the defending AFC champions. Nixon did not practice on Thursday and was limited participation on Friday. Was he taking a rest day on Thursday? “I just hope I’ll be ready to play on Sunday. We’ll see,” Nixon said. The tone of his voice, however, took all the mystery out of it. Five players are out for the Packers, including edge rusher Micah Parsons, who was designated for return this week following last year’s torn ACL. He was limited participation at all three practices this week, an obvious good sign as he anticipates progressing into team drills next week. The four other players who are out are starting linebacker and defensive captain Zaire Franklin (shin), starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle), former starting right guard Travis Glover (knee) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Those players missed all three practices this week. Along with Nixon, running backs Chris Brooks (ankle) and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) are questionable. Brooks was designated for return after missing the last four games; he could be added to the roster on Saturday. The Patriots will be without their top two receivers. Along with former Packers standout Romeo Doubs, who is on injured reserve, star receiver A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) is out. In a potential lift, star tight end Hunter Henry (foot) returned to practice on Friday and is part of a long list of players who are questionable. All of those players practiced on Friday, including starting safety Kevin Byard (chest) and starting cornerback Carlton Davis (neck). Also, All-Pro punt returner Marcus Jones is off the injury report and will play. He did not practice on Thursday. home.blurb: Playing two games in five days may have put additional stress on Brown's knee, Pelissero wrote, but the team is "optimistic" that he could return after the Week 11 bye. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss his second consecutive game due to a knee injury that has hampered him throughout his career, but the team isn't down on his prospects, insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday. The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason, but the results have been underwhelming through the first half of the season. Brown suffered an ankle injury during the team's regular-season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. He returned to action in Week 6, but his knee flared up and caused him to miss Week 8. home.headline: Patriots final Week 9 injury report: Good news, bad news
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Star wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have already been ruled out for the game. The Patriots might also be missing tight end Hunter Henry, who is still battling the foot injury he suffered in last week's win over the Miami Dolphins. Veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins and interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten both returned from injured reserve this week to practice. They are officially listed as questionable to play against the Packers. The New England Patriots will once again be shorthanded on the offensive side of the ball when hosting the Green Bay Packers for a visit on Sunday. But it isn't all bad news for the Patriots. Hollins has been one of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's most reliable downfield targets, and Van Roten was the top replacement at right guard behind Mike Onwenu. Those returns would be a huge lift to a Patriots offense that needs all of the help it can get. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. home.headline: 49ers’ Brandon Aiyuk must jump multiple hurdles before NFL return becomes official
home.blurb: 49ers news: Brandon Aiyuk must jump multiple hurdles before NFL return is official NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics San Francisco 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk faces reinstatement and financial hurdles as his NFL return remains unresolved after talks this week. Add ClutchPoints on Google San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk still faces financial and roster questions after meeting with the team Friday as he pursues a return to the NFL. MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes Aiyuk and newly hired agent Drew Rosenhaus visited the organization’s business offices near Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California. The 28-year-old has remained on the reserve/left squad list since December 2025. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport outlined the obstacles Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, sharing a clip from “The Insiders.” “He did not. Has not officially been reinstated to try to get on the 49ers roster. That has not happened. Now there are several issues here.” From The Insiders on @nflnetwork : Brandon Aiyuk came and went on Friday, exiting the #49ers facility with no resolution. pic.twitter.com/2P7kvXq78w — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 7, 2026 The NFL sent Aiyuk and the NFLPA a letter Thursday regarding bonuses the league says he must repay to the 49ers. Rapoport described a disagreement over the amount. “The NFL believes that is 13 million. The NFLPA believes the number is a little less. We'll see where they land if there's a negotiation.” Aiyuk signed a four-year , $120 million extension before the 2024 season after earning second-team All-Pro honors in 2023. Arbitration could prolong the repayment dispute. He has not played since suffering a multi-ligament knee injury on October 20, 2024. Even reinstatement would not necessarily force an immediate roster move, Rapoport explained. “My understanding is the NFL is expected to give a two-week roster exemption if he gets reinstated, which means the 49ers wouldn't have to do anything immediately anyway.” The trade deadline arrives Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET/1 p.m. PT, but general manager John Lynch has said he does not expect Aiyuk to play for San Francisco again. Neither reinstatement nor the potential exemption would settle where he resumes his career. Josh Davis is an Associate Editor at ClutchPoints with a focus on MLB. This time it is in Seattle. Drew Lock will start at quarterback for Seattle, as Sam Darnold is dealing with quad and rib injuries. Lock beat the Cardinals 31-7 when he started in Week 2, throwing three touchdown passes. For the Cardinals, this time, Gardner Minshew will make the start at quarterback after he led a comeback against the Dallas Cowboys. The Seahawks are 4-4 with three losses to some of the toughest teams in the NFL — the Denver Broncos , San Francisco 49ers and Chicago Bears . As we prepare to watch this matchup, Seahawks Wire lead writer Kole Musgrove gives us some insight to the team he covers, and he gives us his game predictions. He takes us "behind enemy lines". Seahawks injuries and impact The Cardinals already saw a Seahawks team without Sam Darnold, but how do things look differently not only without Darnold, but without left tackle Charles Cross, guard Quenton Nelson, receiver Rashid Shaheed and defensive lineman Leonard Williams? I don't think it's an overstatement to say the Seahawks might have one of their biggest tests of the season. The NFL is a "next man up" caliber league, so Seattle's depth and coaching is going to come on full display on Sunday. I suspect Seattle's gameplan will continue to be conservative, keeping Drew Lock away from difficult situations like the last time he started. What has changed for the Seahawks since they played the Cardinals in Week 2? What has changed has been inconsistent quarterback play. Drew Lock exited and in came Sam Darnold again, as expected. Unfortunately, he has not been the Sam Darnold we saw last year or with the Vikings. In fairness, it's also not the same caliber of coaching, either. Still, Darnold has been outperformed by Drew Lock considerably this year. Sadly for the Cardinals, y'all will be getting the seemingly "better" QB again… at least as far as this year goes. The Cardinals' QB change How does the Cardinals' move from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew look from the perspective of the Seahawks and their fans? We are a little nervous, not going to lie. This is twice now the Seahawks will have to face a backup quarterback in the first week of a start, and we already lost to Marcus Mariota. If there was ever a time for the Cardinals to upset Seattle, this would be it! Arizona's offense looked a lot more explosive with him slinging it, and plenty of Seahawks fans are also Wazzu fans so they are well aware of what Minshew Mania can do. Players to watch Who are the guys to watch for Seattle with so many players down with injuries? I would say this is as good a time as any for Tory Horton to make a name for himself. He has shown flashes of brilliance, but with Lock coming in perhaps the backups will have better connection with one another. Defensively, watch out for Rylie Mills at defensive tackle who will no doubt be filling in for Leonard Williams. Who wins this time, and how does it happen? I'm still picking the Seahawks. Their season feels on the verge of spiraling out of control and I am picking them in a desperation spot. Seattle owns Arizona, but games between these teams are always more competitive at Lumen Field for some reason. The three of the last four games in Seattle have been decided by scores of 16-6, 20-10 and 19-9. So I'm taking the Hawks 18-8. away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Ex-NFL star Antonio Brown avoids jail time as part of plea deal after Miami shooting Winners, losers as Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). away.headline: Seahawks QB Drew Lock to play through severe elbow injury vs Cardinals
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks are set to take on the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 with backup quarterback Drew Lock after starter Sam Darnold was ruled out with a quad injury. However, it turns out Lock is dealing with a bit of a serious injury of his own. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Lock has been battling severe tendinitis in his throwing elbow, but the Seahawks are still comfortable with having him start on Sunday against the Cardinals after he looked good in limited practice reps this week. Brandon Aiyuk Makes Strong Statement on NFL Return Before 49ers Meeting It’s good news that the Seahawks still feel comfortable in Lock’s ability to play and play well this week, but this injury update is certainly a cause for concern, especially because it is affecting his throwing arm. So, it will be worth monitoring up until kickoff on Sunday and even throughout the game because if he is unable to play, the Seahawks would be forced to turn to former 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe. Lock has already filled in quite nicely for Darnold two times this season, completing 35 of his 48 pass attempts for 422 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions, but that was when he was healthy. That could be why the Seahawks are so comfortable with rolling with him this week, though. Every win also matters in the NFC West as Seattle currently sits in second place with a 4-4 record. The San Francisco 49ers are in the top spot at 6-1. A second-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft, Lock has thrown for 6,769 yards, 38 touchdowns and 28 interceptions in his professional career. away.headline: Week 9 Injury Report: Cardinals at Seahawks

Nelson will have what Macdonald described as a "minor procedure" on his knee, and is considered week-to-week, but he will not head to injured reserve. With Nelson out, the Seahawks are moving Grey Zabel back to left guard, his position for the last year and a half before he moved to right guard following the acquisition of Nelson, and Anthony Bradford will return to the starting lineup at right guard. Drew Lock , who will start in place of Darnold, was limited all week due to an elbow injury, but he does not have a game status. In addition to the seven players ruled out, outside linebacker Connor O'Toole is questionable with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. For the Cardinals, left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), right guard Jon Gaines II (ankle) and running back Bam Knight (concussion) have all been ruled out. Guard Isaiah Adams (ankle), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and defensive tackle Walter Nolen III (ankle) are all listed as questionable after being limited in practice on Friday. An NFL analyst doesn't see Sam Darnold's absence as a detriment to the Seattle Seahawks. Darnold will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury, and the defending champions will instead turn to Drew Lock for the Week 9 division showdown. Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci wondered if that switch will actually help Seattle's offense. "I hate to say this: Drew Lock might give the Seahawks a better chance to win at the quarterback position," DiNucci said on CBS Sports' Just Football. Darnold has struggled a year after leading the Seahawks to a Super Bowl title. The 29-year-old has thrown nine interceptions in seven games, with his quarterback rating dipping from 99.1 to 79.5. Meanwhile, Lock led Seattle to a season-opening comeback win off the bench before excelling in a road victory over Arizona. DiNucci suggested that another strong showing against the NFC West opponent could create a quarterback controversy. "Sam Darnold has not played well this year. For whatever reason, he's turning the ball over. This offense looks stuck in the mud," DiNucci said. "I don't want to say this is a soft benching, but Drew Lock -- when he came in relief Week 1 against the New England Patriots -- led that team back. Played really well. High completion percentage, no turnovers. And then Week 2, followed it up against the same Arizona Cardinals team he's gonna play this [week] with 235 yards and three touchdowns. "I'm very intrigued to see what Drew Lock does this weekend. If he plays like he played the first two weeks of the season. I think this is gonna be a very interesting topic the rest of the season."

According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Lock has been battling severe tendinitis in his throwing elbow, but the Seahawks are still comfortable with having him start on Sunday against the Cardinals after he looked good in limited practice reps this week. Brandon Aiyuk Makes Strong Statement on NFL Return Before 49ers Meeting It’s good news that the Seahawks still feel comfortable in Lock’s ability to play and play well this week, but this injury update is certainly a cause for concern, especially because it is affecting his throwing arm. So, it will be worth monitoring up until kickoff on Sunday and even throughout the game because if he is unable to play, the Seahawks would be forced to turn to former 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe. Lock has already filled in quite nicely for Darnold two times this season, completing 35 of his 48 pass attempts for 422 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions, but that was when he was healthy. That could be why the Seahawks are so comfortable with rolling with him this week, though. Every win also matters in the NFC West as Seattle currently sits in second place with a 4-4 record. The San Francisco 49ers are in the top spot at 6-1. A second-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft, Lock has thrown for 6,769 yards, 38 touchdowns and 28 interceptions in his professional career. home.headline: Week 9 Injury Report: Cardinals at Seahawks
home.blurb: In addition to quarterback Sam Darnold , who head coach Mike Macdonald ruled out earlier in the week, the Seahawks will also be without left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), left guard Quenton Nelson (knee), outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), nose tackle Brandon Pili (back), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger). Nelson will have what Macdonald described as a "minor procedure" on his knee, and is considered week-to-week, but he will not head to injured reserve. With Nelson out, the Seahawks are moving Grey Zabel back to left guard, his position for the last year and a half before he moved to right guard following the acquisition of Nelson, and Anthony Bradford will return to the starting lineup at right guard. Drew Lock , who will start in place of Darnold, was limited all week due to an elbow injury, but he does not have a game status. In addition to the seven players ruled out, outside linebacker Connor O'Toole is questionable with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. For the Cardinals, left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), right guard Jon Gaines II (ankle) and running back Bam Knight (concussion) have all been ruled out. Guard Isaiah Adams (ankle), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and defensive tackle Walter Nolen III (ankle) are all listed as questionable after being limited in practice on Friday. G Isaiah Adams (ankle, limited participation) CB Max Melton (knee, limited participation) DT Walter Nolen III (ankle, limited participation) The Seahawks continued their week of preparation ahead of their Week 9 game against the Cardinals with a relatively long list of players not practicing. Given the short week coming off a Monday night game, it's entirely possible that some of the absences are precautionary, but it will be something to watch when the team puts out game statuses on Friday. Two players were new on the injury report, outside linebacker Derick Hall who did not practice due to a back injury, and linebacker Ernest Jones IV , who was limited with an ankle injury. Two players, outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and left guard Quenton Nelson (knee), went from limited Wednesday to not practicing on Thursday. Baker Mayfield and the Bucs won in Week 8 without completing a pass, and after an 0-4 start they’ve won three of their last four games to put themselves right back in the mix to win a terrible NFC South. The Bucs have back-to-back division wins over Carolina and Atlanta, but things will be a lot tougher on the road against the Bears and an MVP candidate in Williams . Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. The Bears have also scored at least 30 points in every game that Williams has completed this season, making them one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Oddsmakers have set Chicago as a six-point favorite at home as it looks to get to 7-2 before a Week 10 bye. The Bears are still behind the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings – who beat them earlier this season – in the NFC North standings. Let’s take a look at the opening odds for this primetime matchup in a loaded Week 9. Buccaneers vs. Bears Odds, Spread and Total for NFL Week 9 Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bucs +6 (-112) Bears -6 (-108) 46.5 (Over -112/Under -108) There hasn’t been any real movement in the odds for this game since they opened on Sunday night, even with the Bears picking up an upset win over Seattle. This is a battle between two very different teams, as Tampa Bay has relied heavily on the running game and its defense to get back in the playoff mix while the Bears are one of the best offenses in football. Chicago ranks 10th in EPA/Play, 11th in success rate and tied for 13th in yards per play this season despite the fact that Williams has missed three full games and part of the team’s Week 2 loss to Minnesota. When the former No. 1 overall pick has been on the field, Ben Johnson’s club has been humming on the offensive end, dropping 34 points in Week 8 against a Seattle defense that is No. 1 in the NFL in success rate and entered Week 8 at No. 1 in yards per play allowed. Tampa Bay’s defense is now No. 1 in EPA/Play after picking off Michael Penix Jr. several times in a rain-soaked matchup in Week 8, but things won’t be nearly as easy against Williams. On the bright side for the Bucs, they should be able to run the ball (eighth in EPA/Rush this season) against a Bears defense that is allowing 4.4 yards per carry in 2026. Chicago traded for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons ahead of Week 8, but the Tampa Bay running game – led by Bucky Irving – won’t be easy to stop on Sunday night. I lean with the Bears to win this game, and it’ll be interesting to see if the odds move at all with both teams trending in the right direction with the halfway point of the 2026 season upon us. The Chicago Bears put the NFL on notice last week. It started with trading for All-Pro defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons, and finished with a statement victory at Seattle on Monday night. The Bears' public perception couldn't be more positive, which is why they're laying almost a touchdown at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football. My Buccaneers vs. Bears predictions put a pin in all that optimism blowing around the Windy City, giving respect to Tampa Bay's turnaround in recent weeks. Here are my NFL picks for SNF on November 8, featuring a fade of Caleb Williams. Buccaneers vs Bears prediction: Buccaneers +6.5 If you check out my weekly NFL underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the pirates and making the Chicago Bears' 8-0 ATS run in prime time walk the plank. Chicago is great, but it has a short week to rest and ready for a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team playing some of the best two-way football in the NFL. After a bumpy start, due to high-variance occurrences, the Bucs have won three of their last four (the loss was in OT) in nasty fashion. Todd Bowles' defense has stepped up during this span, throwing ice on some of the league's top passing playbooks and rating atop the sexy defensive measurements, like EPA and DVOA. On offense, the ground game has ripped up the turf with a Top 5 rushing attack, chowing down on TOP like Malnati's deep dish. Tampa Bay has dominated the football for an average of 35:30 during this stretch, making rival offenses a spectator. The look-ahead line for this SNF pairing was Bucs +5.5 before the Bears' big win on MNF. It has since jumped to +6.5 with the market still pricing Tampa as a losing team. Given the situational squeeze for Chicago and the Bucs' current form, I'm grabbing this inflated spread with the dog. Buccaneers vs Bears combo Tampa Bay isn't getting any respect as the market moves toward Chicago. But the Bears are on a short week and facing a Bucs team playing great two-way football, especially on defense. Baker Mayfield doesn't shrink from the moment. We've seen him make plays in big games, and with the Chicago blitz on his heels, Mayfield runs one into the end zone on SNF. Caleb Williams won't get his normal run on Sunday night with the Bucs' rushing attack putting this game in mud. When he does throw, Williams faces a Tampa Bay pass defense that has already shut down some top air attacks. Projections sit as low as 202 yards from the Chicago QB. They've handed off on 53.5% of snaps in the last four games, utilizing a pace that would make molasses shake its head, burning the fourth most seconds per play clock. picks.headline: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
picks.blurb: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football F1 São Paulo GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Frank Schwab Senior writer Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:01 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud. This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays. Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. picks.headline: Buccaneers at Bears: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: Chicago's rolling with Caleb Williams back. The Bears have won three straight since his return from a hamstring injury, scoring at least 30 points in each game without ever trailing. That includes Monday's 34-17 win in Seattle. Chicago has won those games by an average of 10.3 points. Who needs a passing game? Tampa Bay beat Atlanta 16-0 last week without completing a single pass, rushing for a franchise-record 324 yards. Bucky Irving contributed 170 yards and Kenny Gainwell added 140. That followed a 30-point blowout of the Panthers in which Baker Mayfield only threw for 64 yards, as the ground-attack generated 258 yards. Third-down could decide this one. Chicago's defense has held opponents to a league-best 23.8% conversion rate. Getting Tampa Bay into obvious passing situations would put pressure on an offense with the NFL's lowest team passer rating. Swift enters with momentum. D'Andre Swift scored three second-half rushing touchdowns against Seattle. Chicago's ability to finish drives on the ground gives Williams valuable support near the goal line. Watch the turnaround and the number. Chicago returns from a Monday night road game to host Sunday night. The Bears are favored in the -6/-6.5 range, a sizable margin against a Buccaneers team coming off consecutive wins. Under Ben Johnson, Chicago is 8-1 against the spread in primetime games. Todd Bowles, however, is just 11-18 straight-up and 10-18-1 ATS in that spot as head coach of the Bucs and Jets. Fun fact. Probably not the blueprint you want to carry into every Sunday. Chicago is playing with confidence, Caleb Williams looks increasingly comfortable and Ben Johnson's offense has enough balance to avoid making this entirely about the quarterback. The Buccaneers' defense can absolutely create problems, especially if Williams gets careless under pressure, but I expect Chicago to make Tampa Bay sustain more offense than it needed against Atlanta. The Bears' shorter week after visiting Seattle keeps me from projecting a runaway. Still, they should do enough to win a fourth straight and cover the number. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Bears 31, Buccaneers 16 Todd Bowles might need to conjure another storm to even the playing field. The Buccaneers will surely need more than a 0-3 passing performance from Baker Mayfield to keep up with one of the NFC's most imposing matchups. But it'll be tough for both Mayfield and the run game to ward off Jeffery Simmons, who could once again feast in prime time against a vulnerable interior line. Tampa Bay's defense has picked things up, but slowing Caleb Williams and the rest of Ben Johnson's attack might prove too tall a task for the unit. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Bears 27, Buccaneers 17 Can Baker Mayfield complete a pass? Will he even attempt one? Those are the biggest questions for the visitors, especially against everyone's favorite Super Bowl pick this week. It's not like Chicago hasn't earned that honor though, following a trade for Jeffery Simmons. The star defensive tackle could give the Bucs' running game some trouble and that is bad news for a team that doesn't have enough to keep up with this Bears' offense. Better hop on that bandwagon now because it's about to reach capacity. away.blurb: Is Baker Mayfield Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb in Week 7, and he's off the team's injury report and expected to play in Week 8. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). away.blurb: Running back Kyle Monangai on Friday was back at practice for the first time since suffering a thumb and turf toe injury in Week 4. TOP Pick Bills vs Vikings prediction: Under 44.5 The Minnesota Vikings have flown under the radar as one of the best Under teams in the NFL over the last 12 months. They've hit the Under in 16 of their last 19 games, generating a cool 60% ROI . This 44.5-point total has seen some movement to the Under elsewhere, crossing the key number of 44, and was as high as 47.5 on the lookahead when Kyler Murray was expected under center. I understand Josh Allen is the NFL MVP odds favorite, and he's had success against Brian Flores' defense in the past, posting a 16:2 TD-to-INT ratio over six games. LT Dion Dawkins and LG Alec Anderson both missed practice this week, while RT Spencer Brown missed Week 8 and remains questionable. To make matters worse, Josh Palmer is doubtful, DJ Moore has been limited, and Khalil Shakir was a DNP on Friday for personal reasons. The Bills' defense pressures QBs at the third-highest rate, and this was already a Bottom 5 offense with Murray under center. Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. away.headline: Vikings-Bills First Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday. home.headline: Kyler Murray Injury Update, Latest on Vikings QB's Return Timeline, Severity of Hamstring Strain
home.blurb: Details of Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray's hamstring injury have come out as he will miss at least one game. Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Murray was diagnosed with a Grade 2 hamstring strain that could keep him out beyond just Monday's game against the Buffalo Bills: Injuries have been a theme in the 2026 campaign for Murray. The veteran quarterback suffered a concussion the the first game of the season and was held out of a Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears while remaining in the concussion protocol. Backup Carson Wentz appeared in his stead. "Murray received several medical opinions on the hamstring after last Sunday's loss at Detroit, and the risk of making the injury worse or having Murray alter his style by trying to play this week weren't worth it. So Carson Wentz will start against the Bills, and then the Vikings will reassess Murray's health ahead of their Week 10 NFC North matchup with the Packers." Vikes QB Trade 'On The Table' Pelissero added how Carson Wentz plays against the Bills could impact how Minnesota approaches Murray's rehab because it would be "easier" to be patient if Wentz performs well. And following a Week 8 loss against the Detroit Lions, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed to reporters that Murray was dealing with hamstring soreness and was going through a "full eval," though didn't think his quarterback would miss a Week 9 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. The 29-year-old's first season in Minnesota has been bumpy. While the Vikings (6-1) have been good this season, they've largely been carried by their defense and special teams. Murray has struggled to invigorate the passing offense, posting 1,022 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions through the air this season. "It's just continuing to build that rapport of the plans, the comfort level," O'Connell told reporters after Murray missed connecting with superstar wideout Justin Jefferson in Week 8 on a number of potential big plays, "[and] continuing to implore some input from him on things he likes and things [where] we carve it and make it even cleaner and better for him so that we do get some of that comfort where he'll throw things with anticipation and we get the look for a play, and we all know it's coming, and we see the pitch and catch there." The Vikings will look to get back in the win column after suffering their first loss of the season in Week 8 against the Detroit Lions.
